locator: Water with fuel or toxic chemicals in it
conditions: Suspected fuel, toxic chemicals or radioactive contamination
support: Use a different safe supply. Standard boiling and microbial disinfection do not make this water safe.
limitations: Does not list contaminant-specific lab remediation; applies to emergency consumer decisions only.
conflicts: None across CDC/EPA emergency guidance.
editorial_note: Used as upstream hard-stop gate prior to any field treatment card.

locator: Boil > Steps for boiling water
conditions: Microbiologically suspect water with acceptable chemical source; portable heat and safe vessel
support: Clarify cloudy water first. Rolling boil for one minute; above 6,500 feet for three minutes. Cool and cover in sanitized containers.
limitations: Does not remove dissolved metals, nitrates, fuel, or cyanotoxins.
conflicts: Older Track B B009 omitted the 6,500 ft threshold; CDC threshold governs.
editorial_note: Require explicit timer verification after rolling boil starts.

locator: Rainwater might not be safe for household use
conditions: Collected rain, including apparently clean runoff
support: Germs and chemicals can enter from air, roof, gutters or storage. Prefer safe drinking water for ingestion.
limitations: Site-specific roof and atmospheric chemistry vary; no universal roof-wash formula assumed.
conflicts: None; aligns with CDC potable-first hierarchy.
editorial_note: Separates catchment from raw storage and microbial treatment.

locator: Water treatment methods > Filter and disinfect
conditions: Untreated backcountry water; suitable devices and directions
support: Filter capability varies. Filtering then disinfecting addresses gaps left by typical portable filters. Follow both manufacturers' directions.
limitations: Effectiveness depends on pore rating, cartridge integrity, and manufacturer-verified test standards.
conflicts: None; consumer claims outside NSF/EPA standards are excluded.
editorial_note: Used to require multi-barrier pairing rather than relying on one filter alone.

locator: Disinfect; Using light
conditions: Matched product, concentration, dose, contact time and source condition
support: Chemical disinfection is less dependable against some parasites. UV needs clear water and a correctly used device.
limitations: Cold temperature and organic turbidity reduce chemical efficacy and UV penetration.
conflicts: None; exact manufacturer label governs dose and wait time.
editorial_note: Prohibits improvised chemical dosing when labels are absent.

locator: How to store emergency water; Safe storage containers
conditions: Potable water intended for emergency storage
support: Prefer sealed commercial water or clean food-grade tight-closing containers. Avoid containers that held toxic chemicals.
limitations: Container shelf durability and rotation depend on plastic/material type and storage heat.
conflicts: None; reinforces strict raw-vs-clean segregation.
editorial_note: Used to enforce labeling and dedicated raw/potable vessel separation.

locator: Boil water; Do not drink; Do not use
conditions: Public-water system advisories
support: The notice determines safe activities. Use another source for do-not-drink notices. Do not use tap water for any purpose under a do-not-use notice unless authorities direct otherwise.
limitations: Local utility directives supersede general field summaries.
conflicts: None; exact advisory category is authoritative.
editorial_note: Distinguishes boil-water, do-not-drink, and do-not-use actions explicitly.

locator: Boil > Steps for boiling water > cloudy water
conditions: Cloudy water with no identified chemical hazard
support: Settling or cloth clarification only prepares water for treatment. Do not count it as disinfection.
limitations: Removes coarse suspended solids only; dissolved toxins and microbes remain.
conflicts: Contradicts folklore claims that sand/cloth straining yields potable water; CDC governs.
editorial_note: Always depicted upstream of microbial treatment with an explicit barrier line.

locator: Overview and water treatment methods
conditions: Hiking or camping where no safe source is confirmed
support: Even clear water can contain germs. Assess the supply and carry safe water or an appropriate treatment method.
limitations: Visual clarity never detects microbes or dissolved chemical contaminants.
conflicts: None across CDC/NPS/EPA sources.
editorial_note: Reinforces clarity-is-not-potability invariant across all Z04 cards.

locator: Disinfect; Who should avoid water disinfected with iodine
conditions: Backcountry water with acceptable chemical source; label-directed treatment
support: Avoid iodine-treated drinking water during pregnancy, with thyroid problems or known iodine hypersensitivity. Chlorine and iodine are unreliable against some parasites.
limitations: Not intended for prolonged multi-week use even in healthy adults; check product label.
conflicts: None; aligns with CDC backcountry guidance.
editorial_note: Mandates user medical screening before choosing iodine disinfection.

locator: Using light
conditions: Portable UV disinfection device on a supported batch size of clear water
support: Cloudiness interferes with UV. Use the device's stated volume, mixing and cycle instructions.
limitations: Battery failure, cold battery voltage drop, or container UV opacity can silently defeat treatment.
conflicts: None; requires pre-clarification for turbid sources.
editorial_note: Requires verifying clarity, rated volume, and completed cycle indicator.

locator: Emergency Disinfection of Drinking Water > Bleach
conditions: Emergency water when boiling is unavailable; unscented 5%–9% liquid household chlorine bleach
support: Use one complete current public health protocol for the exact product and water conditions. The EPA instructions specify unscented bleach concentration tables and a minimum contact time; local directions take precedence.
limitations: Ineffective against Cryptosporidium and chemical/fuel contaminants; bleach degrades with age and heat.
conflicts: EPA and CDC both note 8 drops (about 1/8 tsp) per gallon for clear water with 5%–9% bleach; exact concentration on current bottle governs.
editorial_note: Requires reading the bottle label rather than memorizing a single drop count for unknown concentrations.

locator: Cleaning and sanitizing a water storage container before use
conditions: Reusable food-grade water storage containers before filling with potable water
support: Wash with dish soap and warm water, sanitize interior surfaces with a labeled dilute bleach solution for at least 30 seconds, and rinse with safe water before filling.
limitations: Damaged, cracked, or chemical-contaminated containers cannot be rehabilitated by washing.
conflicts: None; complements CDC-S container rules.
editorial_note: Separates routine washing from sanitizing and air-drying/rinsing.

locator: How Much Water to Store; Rotation
conditions: Household emergency water reserve planning
support: Plan at least 1 gallon per person per day for at least 3 days (more for heat, illness, pregnancy, or pets); rotate self-filled water every 6 months.
limitations: Backcountry active travel demands vary sharply by exertion, temperature, and humidity.
conflicts: None; household baseline is cited only as a planning floor, not a physiological maximum.
editorial_note: Distinguishes household storage floors from active field hydration demands.

locator: Cyanotoxins and water treatment
conditions: Surface water with discolored scum, mats, foul odor, or active HAB advisory
support: Do not use a suspect bloom as a drinking-water source. Routine field microbial treatment is not a validated method of removing cyanotoxins.
limitations: Cyanotoxins can persist in visually clear water after a bloom dissipates.
conflicts: Contradicts naive boil-everything advice; CDC/EPA HAB warnings explicitly prohibit boiling HAB water.
editorial_note: Establishes HABs as a chemical-toxin rejection trigger, not a microbial boil target.

locator: Can I boil my water to make it safe to drink?
conditions: Suspected cyanotoxins or applicable do-not-drink water advisory
support: Boiling does not remove cyanotoxins and can increase their concentration. Follow the advisory and use an approved alternate source.
limitations: Do not infer treatment capability or absence of toxin from visual appearance.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Supports regional Upper Midwest lake/pond source screening in summer and autumn.

locator: Blue-green algae and harmful algal blooms
conditions: Minnesota lakes and ponds during warm summer and early autumn
support: Blue-green algae blooms can form quickly along downwind shorelines; keep people and animals out of suspect water and use alternative drinking supplies.
limitations: Local bloom distribution shifts rapidly with wind and wave action.
conflicts: None; reinforces regional Upper Midwest applicability.
editorial_note: Links downwind shoreline accumulation to site-selection and water-source rejection.
reviewer: Regional water quality and public health

locator: How to Disinfect Wells After an Emergency > Safety precautions and before returning to use
conditions: Private drinking water wells submerged or impacted by floodwater
support: Do not drink flood-impacted well water; rely on bottled or verified safe water, watch for fuel/chemical spills, and use qualified well contractors for inspection, electrical safety, and disinfection.
limitations: Well shock-chlorination is unsafe to improvise around damaged electrical equipment or chemical releases.
conflicts: None; aligns with EPA private-well guidance.
editorial_note: Prevents DIY well repair or consumption before testing confirms safety.

locator: Drinking water and preventing infection while hiking or camping
conditions: Untreated surface water in wilderness and rural watersheds
support: Use boiling or a parasite-rated filter. Chemical treatment effectiveness depends on product, target organism, temperature and contact time.
limitations: Pore size alone does not protect if cartridge seals leak or freeze-crack.
conflicts: None; underscores why chemical-only treatment has parasite limits.
editorial_note: Clarifies why filter micron/NSF ratings matter for protozoa.

locator: Removing parasites; Check the filter label
conditions: Surface water impacted by wildlife, livestock, or runoff
support: For parasite removal look for absolute pore size one micron or smaller or a specific certified cyst reduction/removal claim. NSF/ANSI 53 or 58 without the cyst claim does not establish that capability.
limitations: Does not establish removal of viruses, dissolved chemicals or all other hazards.
conflicts: Clarifies gap left by single-barrier chlorine disinfection.
editorial_note: Core evidence for filter-plus-disinfect multi-barrier design in Z04.

locator: Check filter label for which germs and chemicals it removes; filter types
conditions: Exact point-of-use model and a known target
support: Verify the named independently tested reduction claim for the model. A treatment type or general standard number does not establish reduction for a different contaminant.
limitations: Compare the product label and actual conditions; follow the active water advisory.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Frames equipment selection around verified contaminant classes and certifications.

locator: National Primary Drinking Water Regulations
conditions: Surface or groundwater near agriculture, industry, mines, roads, or old plumbing
support: Regulated drinking-water hazards span inorganic chemicals (lead, arsenic, nitrate), organic solvents, pesticides, radionuclides, and microbes; microbial treatments do not remove dissolved inorganic or organic chemicals.
limitations: Field observation cannot measure dissolved chemical concentration; laboratory testing is required.
conflicts: None; underpins strict chemical-rejection boundaries.
editorial_note: Explains why agricultural runoff, mine tailings, and road salt/fuel require source rejection.

locator: Drinking Water Contaminants
conditions: Minnesota surface and groundwater sources
support: Agricultural nitrates, industrial chemicals, road runoff, and naturally occurring minerals can affect local water independent of visual clarity or microbial load.
limitations: Specific contaminant risk varies by county, aquifer, and watershed land use.
conflicts: None; regionalized extension of EPA-CONTAM.
editorial_note: Anchors Upper Midwest watershed and land-use source screening.

locator: Turbidity and Water · optical definition and causes
conditions: Cloudy, silt-laden, or storm-runoff streams and lakes
support: Turbidity measures light scattering. Clay, silt and organic or biological material can contribute to turbidity.
limitations: The USGS measurement is not evidence of potability, actual device clogging, or shielding magnitude. Follow validated treatment guidance.
conflicts: None; supports physical mechanism of pre-clarification.
editorial_note: Explains physical failure of filters and UV in turbid storm runoff.

locator: Snowmelt Runoff and the Water Cycle · runoff
conditions: Late-winter and spring snowpack runoff and melting snow
support: Melting snow can contribute to runoff and streamflow. The observed result varies with watershed, weather and upstream conditions.
limitations: This source does not establish a safe crossing hour, a contamination level or a universal meltwater hydrograph.
conflicts: None; reinforces snow source screening and seasonal runoff shifts.
editorial_note: Supports seasonal snow/ice water cards and meltwater screening.

locator: Two Ways to Purify Water
conditions: Backcountry water treatment planning in National Parks
support: Boiling and chemical/filtration methods each have fuel, time, weight, and organism-coverage trade-offs; match the primary method and backup to route conditions and follow directions.
limitations: Does not resolve chemical spills or algal toxins.
conflicts: Aligns with CDC-T altitude and parasite limits.
editorial_note: Supports primary-plus-backup water treatment selection in Z04.

locator: Emergency Disinfection > Taste and Aeration
conditions: Boiled water after cooling in a clean covered container
support: Boiled water can taste flat from dissolved oxygen loss; pouring between two clean sanitized containers or resting covered improves palatability without re-exposing to raw sources.
limitations: Open transfer in dusty or unsanitary surroundings risks recontamination.
conflicts: None; strictly optional palatability step after cooling.
editorial_note: Ensures aeration uses only sanitized clean-side vessels.

locator: Water filtration FAQ > filter freezing
conditions: Sawyer wet hollow-fiber filters; other models follow their exact manufacturer instructions
support: Freezing can damage a wetted filter. Sawyer advises replacing a filter suspected of freezing; visual inspection cannot establish its integrity.
limitations: Do not extrapolate replacement or integrity-testing instructions to other products without their manuals.
conflicts: None; critical cold-weather filter failure mechanism.
editorial_note: Drives cold-weather filter protection and failure-recognition cards.

locator: Use safe water for drinking, brushing teeth and food preparation
conditions: Applicable emergency-water advice and permissible uses under active local advisory
support: Use confirmed safe water for oral and food-contact tasks. Follow current local instructions for each use.
limitations: Infant formula requires separate P26 conditions. Wound care requires the appropriate care source.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Separates potable-required tasks from non-potable utility uses.

locator: Collecting Rainwater > First-Flush, Debris, and Storage Hygiene
conditions: Improvised or dedicated rainwater catchment systems
support: Bird droppings, windblown dust, leaf tannins, and surface coatings enter initial runoff; isolate collection surfaces, screen coarse debris on the raw side, and treat before drinking.
limitations: Even screened rain catchment remains raw water until validated microbial treatment is applied.
conflicts: None; prevents treating screened rain as potable.
editorial_note: Supports catchment geometry, leaf/branch runoff limits, and first-flush separation.

locator: Fire danger and burning restrictions map and links
conditions: Current Minnesota location, date and jurisdiction
support: Check current restrictions and local authority requirements before lighting.
limitations: Restrictions can change daily with humidity, wind, and drought; verify immediately before use.
conflicts: None; local jurisdiction always supersedes general notes.
editorial_note: Mandatory legal check before any live fire card.
reviewer: Fire prevention and local land management

locator: Build your campfire; choose a location
conditions: Where campfires are currently permitted
support: Use an established fire ring where required or available. Protect the area from nearby combustible materials, avoid windy conditions and keep water ready.
limitations: Site clearances vary by fuel load, slope, and wind; no universal safe radius fits all terrain.
conflicts: None; aligns with USFS-FIRE.
editorial_note: Grounds site-selection and ring-preparation procedures.

locator: Build your campfire > Tinder, kindling, fuel
conditions: Outdoor authorized campfire
support: Dry tinder, small kindling and larger fuel serve different roles. Gather materials before ignition. Avoid accelerants.
limitations: Species availability and moisture content vary by season and local collection rules.
conflicts: None; separates material function from unverified species claims.
editorial_note: Used to stage three-tier fuel geometry without prescribing specific live trees.

locator: Maintain and extinguish a campfire
conditions: Occupied campfire, water and tools available
support: Stay with the fire. Drown, stir and add water again until cool. Leaving visible embers or merely covering them is unsafe.
limitations: Deep duff or peat soils can hold smoldering embers underground even after surface ash cools.
conflicts: None; prohibits dirt-only burial as primary extinguishment.
editorial_note: Enforces drown-stir-feel-cold cycle before site departure.

locator: Carbon monoxide poisoning from portable camping equipment
conditions: Tents, campers, vehicles and other enclosed spaces
support: Fuel-burning camping equipment can lead to fatal carbon monoxide buildup in enclosed spaces.
limitations: High altitude increases incomplete combustion and CO production.
conflicts: None; aligns with CDC-CO and NPS guidance.
editorial_note: Hard-stop prohibition against indoor/vestibule/tent combustion.
reviewer: Carbon monoxide safety and emergency medicine

locator: Prevent CO poisoning > Portable generators
conditions: Portable fuel-driven generator during an outage
support: Use outdoors at least 20 feet from the home with exhaust directed away from buildings.
limitations: Wind eddies, overhanging eaves, and open windows can still draw exhaust toward occupied structures.
conflicts: None; 20 ft is a minimum floor, not a guarantee in enclosed alleys.
editorial_note: Anchored numeric separation rule for portable generators only.

locator: CO poisoning symptoms; what to do if suspected
conditions: Suspected carbon monoxide exposure
support: Escape to fresh air immediately and contact emergency services. Symptoms can include headache, dizziness, nausea and confusion.
limitations: CO is colorless and odorless; symptoms mimic viral illness or altitude fatigue and can incapacitate sleepers without waking.
conflicts: None; aligns with CDC-CO.
editorial_note: Standard CO emergency stop condition across Z02 and Z03.
reviewer: Carbon monoxide safety and emergency medicine

locator: Outside > If there is no shelter nearby
conditions: Stranded outdoors during a winter storm
support: Seek shelter and block wind and wet exposure. Reduce heat loss from contact with snow or ground.
limitations: Does not guarantee overnight survival without adequate insulation or rescue.
conflicts: None; reinforces no-fire exposure control priority.
editorial_note: Anchors no-fire fallback when ignition fails or is banned.

locator: Installing and maintaining CO alarms
conditions: U.S. household CO prevention
support: Install CO alarms on every level and outside sleeping areas. Follow placement and maintenance instructions.
limitations: Alarms alert to buildup after release begins; they never make indoor fuel-burning appliances safe.
conflicts: None; complements C05 and C06.
editorial_note: Paired with exit-plan checks in household and shelter cards.

locator: What > Firemaking with flint and steel
conditions: Historical hard stone and suitable steel demonstration
support: With traditional flint-and-steel, the flint removes small particles of steel that oxidize in air; a receptive tinder material catches the hot particles.
limitations: Requires high-carbon steel and sharp hard rock (e.g., chert/flint); random unknown rocks fail and can fracture dangerously.
conflicts: Corrects common misconception that sparks come from the rock itself.
editorial_note: Used for mechanism diagrams and cold-inspection teaching cards.

locator: Fire and illumination
conditions: Outdoor emergency kit
support: Carry a dependable ignition option and protect it from moisture. Carry a separate light.
limitations: Disposable butane lighters lose vapor pressure in freezing cold; matches fail when damp.
conflicts: None; supports redundant dry ignition kit planning.
editorial_note: Keeps lighting independent of fire-building.

locator: Background and Procedure > Bow Drill
conditions: Interpretive demonstration using known materials
support: Reciprocating motion turns a spindle against a hearth. Friction heats wood dust until it can sustain an ember.
limitations: Moisture, resinous wood, poor notch geometry, or physical fatigue can prevent ember formation.
conflicts: Does not guarantee ignition in emergency field conditions; conceptual/supervised training only.
editorial_note: Clearly distinguishes cold mechanism instruction from field-validated emergency ignition.

locator: Know Before You Go > Campfire Safety and Restrictions
conditions: National Forest and public lands with seasonal fire restrictions
support: Fire restriction stages progressively limit open campfires and may permit only liquid/gas stoves with an on/off shutoff valve in cleared areas; check current local orders before departure.
limitations: Exact Stage 1/2/3 definitions vary by forest unit and state agency.
conflicts: None; aligns with MN-FIRE.
editorial_note: Supports fire-restriction tier decision trees and stove vs campfire distinctions.

locator: Know Before You Go > Extinguish and Site Clearance
conditions: Authorized outdoor campfire on mineral soil
support: Clear flammable grass, needles, and twigs down to mineral soil before building a small fire, keep flames away from overhanging branches, and confirm cold ash before leaving.
limitations: Root systems and organic duff beneath shallow clearing can ignite invisibly.
conflicts: None; aligns with SMOKEY C02/C04.
editorial_note: Underpins mineral-soil cutaway and underground root-fire failure cards.

locator: Wildland Fire Safety > Campfires and Stoves
conditions: Outdoor cooking with portable liquid or canister stoves
support: Operate stoves on level cleared ground away from tents and dry fuels, cool completely before refueling, and move away from any spilled fuel before lighting.
limitations: Fuel canisters behave differently in cold weather and high elevation; follow manufacturer limits.
conflicts: None; aligns with CPSC-C and USFS-FIRE.
editorial_note: Governs stove setup, refueling isolation, and spill failure recognition.
reviewer: Portable appliance safety and fire prevention

locator: Carbon Monoxide Poisoning Basics > Sources and Prevention
conditions: Any enclosed or semi-enclosed structure, garage, porch, tent, or vehicle
support: Never burn charcoal, operate camp stoves, or run fuel-burning heaters inside homes, garages, tents, or vehicles even with doors or windows partly open.
limitations: Vent cracks and open garage doors do not prevent lethal CO accumulation.
conflicts: Refutes dangerous myth that cracking a tent vent or garage door makes indoor combustion safe.
editorial_note: Hard-stop rule across all Z02 ventilation and Z03 combustion cards.
reviewer: Carbon monoxide safety and emergency medicine

locator: Principle 5 > Minimize Campfire Impacts
conditions: Permitted backcountry sites where wood fires are allowed
support: Where fires are permitted, keep fires small, use only dead and downed wood gathered lawfully, burn wood completely to ash, and use a camp stove where wood is scarce or impacts are high.
limitations: Some parks prohibit all wood gathering or open fires regardless of deadfall availability.
conflicts: None; balances lawful fuel collection with habitat protection.
editorial_note: Guides lawful fuel gathering and small-fire thermal management.

locator: Red Flag Warning and Fire Weather Watch Definitions
conditions: Local fire weather outlook and land-manager order
support: A Red Flag Warning means local conditions support extreme fire danger. Check local criteria and restrictions and adjust plans.
limitations: A wind advisory alone is not a Red Flag Warning or an ignition permit.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Establishes Red Flag / high-wind conditions as automatic no-fire triggers.

locator: Wildfires > Stay Safe and Smoke Protection
conditions: Approaching wildfire or heavy smoke in camp or community
support: Evacuate early along open routes per official orders, protect airways from heavy smoke, and avoid turning back into active fire corridors.
limitations: Cloth face coverings do not filter fine wildfire smoke particles; fitted particulate respirators or clean indoor air are distinct interventions.
conflicts: None; coordinates with NWS-WILDFIRE.
editorial_note: Covers wildfire escape and smoke decision thresholds in Z01/Z03.

locator: Minnesota State Park Rules > Firewood and Fires
conditions: Minnesota state parks and public campgrounds
support: Build fires only in designated rings where permitted and use only approved local or certified firewood to prevent invasive forest-pest spread.
limitations: Rules differ between state parks, state forests, and federal wilderness areas; verify unit rules.
conflicts: None; regionalized legal compliance for Minnesota.
editorial_note: Documents lawful wood sourcing and designated-ring constraints.

locator: Before your trip and while visiting
conditions: State-forest travel and backcountry planning
support: Know the route, check conditions, carry navigation and safety equipment and share trip details.
limitations: Conditions and trail maintenance vary seasonally across forest units.
conflicts: None; aligns with NPS-H.
editorial_note: Foundation for trip planning and pre-departure risk checks.
reviewer: Land management and search and rescue

locator: Navigation; insulation; emergency shelter; emergency food and water
conditions: Outdoor trips; adjust kit to season and route
support: Carry essential systems including navigation, insulation, light, water and emergency shelter.
limitations: Carrying items without practice or cold-weather verification does not ensure readiness.
conflicts: None; baseline kit system architecture.
editorial_note: Supports failure-mode packing and kit verification cards.
reviewer: Field education and search and rescue

locator: Finding a campsite
conditions: Legal established or designated campsite
support: Choose a durable legal site suited to the conditions. Campsite rules and physical risks vary by park.
limitations: Established sites can still develop new hazard trees or flood risk after storms.
conflicts: None; requires live site inspection even at designated pads.
editorial_note: First gate of shelter site selection.

locator: Before and during camping; know your surroundings
conditions: Stream valleys and runoff channels subject to flash flooding
support: Choose higher ground away from water channels. Rain far upstream can drive rapid flooding.
limitations: Dry streambeds and gentle swales can flood rapidly without local rainfall.
conflicts: None; aligns with NWS-FLOOD.
editorial_note: Core hydrological exclusion rule for shelter placement.

locator: Outside and find shelter
conditions: Cold, wet or windy winter conditions
support: Block wind, stay dry and keep off cold ground. Keep exposure reduction separate from making a fire.
limitations: Improvised windbreaks do not provide rated thermal protection or snow-load capacity.
conflicts: None; aligns with CDC-H.
editorial_note: Separates wind, ground, and moisture heat-loss pathways.

locator: Recognizing and treating hypothermia
conditions: Cold wet exposure; signs such as confusion, slurred speech, fumbling or drowsiness
support: Suspected hypothermia warrants prompt help and protection from further cooling. It can occur above freezing if wet or chilled.
limitations: Early mild shivering can mask rapidly worsening judgment impairment.
conflicts: None; aligns with ARC and WMS guidance.
editorial_note: Anchors exposure-to-medical escalation thresholds.

locator: If you hear thunder; when it is safe to return
conditions: Thunderstorm and reachable substantial building or enclosed hard-topped vehicle
support: Move to proper shelter at thunder. Wait 30 minutes after last thunder before resuming outdoor activity.
limitations: Fabric tents, open pavilions, and trees are not lightning-safe shelters.
conflicts: None; 30-minute rule is standard NWS guidance.
editorial_note: Separates weather cover from lightning protection in Z02.

locator: Protect yourself from heat
conditions: Outdoor activity in hot conditions
support: Limit exertion in hot periods, take breaks in cooler places and monitor for illness.
limitations: High humidity reduces sweat evaporation and raises heat strain at lower air temperatures.
conflicts: None; aligns with NWS-HEAT and NIOSH-H.
editorial_note: Anchors shade, pacing, and hot-weather shelter selection.

locator: Insulation; Emergency Shelter
conditions: Weather, terrain and expected overnight risk
support: Extra clothing and usable emergency shelter belong in the route-specific kit.
limitations: Emergency bivies and space blankets trap condensation and tear easily if misused.
conflicts: None; requires inspecting and practicing shelter deployment.
editorial_note: Supports overnight emergency shelter readiness.

locator: Outside > Protect yourself from frostbite and hypothermia
conditions: Outdoor winter storm
support: Keep clothing dry and avoid overexertion. Wetness accelerates cooling.
limitations: Cotton retains moisture and accelerates conductive and evaporative heat loss.
conflicts: None; reinforces moisture-management layering.
editorial_note: Links sweat management to overnight insulation integrity.

locator: Plan your hike; Stay together
conditions: Groups on hiking routes
support: Choose a route suited to the group's abilities and hike at a pace that keeps the group together.
limitations: Fast hikers moving ahead at junctions is a leading driver of preventable separation.
conflicts: None; aligns with SAR prevention principles.
editorial_note: Core reference for group accountability and pacing cards.
reviewer: Group leaders and search and rescue

locator: Ice Safety > basic precautions
conditions: Minnesota ice edges and travel routes
support: No ice is universally safe. Strength can differ over short distances; appearance or tracks alone cannot establish a safe crossing.
limitations: Currents, springs, snow insulation, and freeze-thaw cycles weaken ice invisibly.
conflicts: None; mandates shore-bound detour for foundational walking parties.
editorial_note: Maintains strict separation from specialized B013 ice chapters.
reviewer: Ice safety and search and rescue

locator: What You Can Do to Reduce Risk
conditions: Forest campsites and stops
support: Look for dead trees and falling material. Stay away from hazardous trees and move away when winds make the site unsafe.
limitations: Internal decay and root rot can cause live-looking trees to fail in saturated soils or high wind.
conflicts: Does not specify a universal exclusion radius; tree height and slope govern fall reach.
editorial_note: Prevents false precision on fall-zone distance while requiring overhead screening.

locator: In vehicles during a winter storm
conditions: Vehicle stranded in winter weather with no immediate vehicle hazard
support: Stay with the vehicle if a safe nearby destination is not obvious. Make the vehicle visible and notify others when possible.
limitations: Snow-blocked exhaust pipes create rapid lethal CO hazards if an engine is run.
conflicts: None; keeps shelter decision distinct from idling engine advice.
editorial_note: Used for stranded-vehicle shelter and exhaust-hazard checks.
reviewer: Winter response and carbon monoxide safety

locator: Cold Weather Safety > Wind Chill and Dressing for Cold
conditions: Cold, windy conditions where exposed skin cools rapidly
support: Wind removes the thin warm air boundary layer around skin and permeable fabrics, sharply accelerating heat loss and frostbite onset; windproof outer shells and sheltered microclimates mitigate convective loss.
limitations: Wind chill charts apply to exposed skin and do not change freezing point of water or equipment.
conflicts: None; clarifies physical mechanism of convective heat loss.
editorial_note: Supports wind-block geometry, shell layering, and wind-chill risk decisions.

locator: Wind Safety > High Wind Hazards
conditions: Forecast or developing high winds, squalls, or straight-line winds
support: High winds topple trees, loft debris, and stress lightweight shelters beyond fabric and anchor limits; relocate out of timbered fall zones and into substantial shelter before gusts peak.
limitations: Tents and tarps lack standardized wind-speed survival guarantees across soil types and pitch angles.
conflicts: None; avoids unvalidated mph ratings for improvised pitches.
editorial_note: Drives high-wind shelter inspection, guying limits, and abandonment thresholds.

locator: During a Tornado: home, outside, vehicle
conditions: Tornado warning; sturdy shelter may be unavailable
support: Prefer the suitable lowest interior area of a sturdy building. If unreachable, use NWS location-specific last-resort guidance and avoid overpasses and flood-prone low ground.
limitations: The branch is contextual. Never portray a ditch, vehicle or makeshift shelter as reliably safe.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Establishes severe-storm abandonment threshold for camp shelters.

locator: Thunderstorm Safety > Hail, Downbursts, and Flooding
conditions: Approaching severe thunderstorm with hail, outflow gusts, or heavy rain
support: Outflow gusts, hail, lightning, and flash runoff can strike before rain arrives at camp; break exposed ridge travel early and secure or vacate lightweight shelters.
limitations: Storm cells can intensify faster than backcountry foot travel can clear exposed terrain.
conflicts: None; integrates with E04 and E07.
editorial_note: Connects storm-structure warning cues to early shelter selection.

locator: Heat Safety Resources · vulnerability and linked protective actions
conditions: High temperature and humidity outdoors
support: Use current heat alerts and reduce exposure or seek cooled shelter when conditions warrant.
limitations: This landing page does not quantify tent warming or universal evaporative cooling. See D21 for the bounded indoor fan guidance.
conflicts: None; aligns with CDC-HEAT and READY-HEAT.
editorial_note: Drives warm-weather tarp/shade configuration and ventilation cards.

locator: Camping: What to Bring > Shelter and Sleep System
conditions: Overnight camping across three-season and cool conditions
support: Match tent/tarp, groundsheet, sleeping pad, and sleeping bag ratings to expected night lows and precipitation; test pitching and inspect poles, zippers, and stakes before departure.
limitations: Manufacturer comfort ratings assume dry insulation, ground pad use, and adequate caloric intake.
conflicts: None; reinforces pre-trip inspection and dry-sleep separation.
editorial_note: Anchors manufactured shelter selection, groundsheet fit, and gear readiness.

locator: Know Before You Go: Camping > Site Selection and Safety
conditions: Dispersed and developed National Forest camping
support: Verify site legality, distance from water, wildlife food-storage rules, and weather exposure; leave fragile vegetation undisturbed and avoid digging drainage trenches where prohibited.
limitations: Dispersed camping rules vary sharply by forest and wilderness designation.
conflicts: Prohibits legacy trenching practices that damage soils and still fail in heavy runoff.
editorial_note: Replaces obsolete ditch-digging advice with slope/drainage site selection.

locator: Principle 2 > Travel and Camp on Durable Surfaces
conditions: Campsite selection and shelter setup on public lands
support: Pitch shelters on established pads, rock, gravel, dry grass, or snow rather than fragile meadows or saturated shorelines; do not alter terrain or cut live vegetation for shelter frames.
limitations: Deadfall shelter construction is inappropriate in high-use or protected zones except genuine life-safety emergencies.
conflicts: Restricts destructive improvised shelter building during routine trips.
editorial_note: Separates lawful low-impact practice from emergency improvised cover.

locator: Avalanche Encyclopedia > Terrain, Slopes, and Runout Zones
conditions: Winter travel and camping in snowy sloped or mountain terrain
support: Avalanches can initiate on slopes roughly 30 to 45 degrees and travel far into flatter runout zones below; avoid camping beneath steep snow slopes, cornices, or gullies without formal avalanche training and current forecasts.
limitations: Gentle flat valley floors can still sit inside runout paths beneath steeper upper slopes.
conflicts: None; strictly excludes unvalidated snow-shelter placement in avalanche terrain.
editorial_note: Enforces avalanche-terrain exclusion on all winter shelter cards.

locator: What to Know; Shelter in Place; Next steps
conditions: External airborne chemical release; officials advise sheltering
support: Follow local instructions for shelter versus evacuation, stopping outside air intake, selecting a room, sealing if directed and awaiting all-clear.
limitations: Tornado, flood, internal gas, fire and CO decisions require their own guidance.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Bridges Z02 shelter selection with emergency-management hazard classes.

locator: Winter Weather > Stay Safe During Winter Storms
conditions: Extreme cold, drifting snow, and power or travel disruption
support: Prepare layered clothing, emergency shelter/heat alternatives, and vehicle winter kits; stay indoors during blizzards, protect against frostbite/hypothermia, and keep exhaust vents and exits clear of drifting snow.
limitations: Drifting snow can block tent vents, doors, and vehicle tailpipes silently overnight.
conflicts: None; reinforces overnight exit/vent clearance checks.
editorial_note: Supports snow-drift exit maintenance and winter shelter failure recognition.

locator: Extreme Heat > Stay Safe in Extreme Heat
conditions: Prolonged heat waves and high overnight temperatures
support: Use ventilated shade, hydration, light breathable clothing, and cooling centers when available; monitor vulnerable companions continuously for heat exhaustion or heat stroke.
limitations: Shaded tarps reduce radiant load but cannot replace medical cooling when core temperature rises.
conflicts: None; aligns with CDC-HEAT and NWS-HEAT.
editorial_note: Supports hot-weather shelter orientation and heat-stress stop conditions.

locator: Responsible Recreation > Preparedness and Wildlife Safety
conditions: Backcountry camps in bear and wildlife country
support: Store food, scented items, and cooking gear separately from sleeping shelters according to local land-agency rules to prevent wildlife intrusions into sleeping areas.
limitations: Required storage method (bear canister, locker, hang) varies by jurisdiction.
conflicts: None; keeps cooking and food odors separate from shelter enclosures.
editorial_note: Connects camp layout, odor separation, and shelter safety.

locator: First Aid Steps > Check the scene; check the person
conditions: Lay responder in United States; assess safety before contact
support: Check scene safety, responsiveness, breathing and immediately life-threatening conditions.
limitations: Lay guidance does not replace advanced clinical or rescue protocols.
conflicts: None; universal first-response opening gate.
editorial_note: Anchors scene-safety-first rule across Z01.

locator: First Aid Steps > Call 9-1-1
conditions: Lay emergency response to unresponsiveness, abnormal breathing or severe bleeding
support: Activate EMS and get needed equipment. Follow dispatcher directions and act within training.
limitations: Remote locations may delay EMS arrival, requiring sustained stabilization after activation.
conflicts: None; aligns with NPS-E.
editorial_note: Mandates early emergency activation and dispatcher adherence.

locator: Warning signs; What to do
conditions: Cold exposure and suspected hypothermia
support: Confusion, slurred speech and drowsiness are warning signs. Obtain medical attention and protect from further cold.
limitations: Shivering may stop as hypothermia worsens; absence of shivering is not reassurance.
conflicts: None; aligns with WMS cold guidelines.
editorial_note: Core neurological red-flag trigger for stopping activity and calling rescue.

locator: Field treatment scenarios and Table 1
conditions: Suspected frostbite outside immediate medical care
support: Avoid refreezing. Whether to actively thaw depends on ability to keep tissue thawed and evacuate. Detailed treatment requires clinical review.
limitations: Field assessment cannot reliably determine final tissue depth.
conflicts: Supersedes outdated rubbing or snow-pack thawing myths.
editorial_note: Retained for cross-zone cold-injury stop boundaries.

locator: Heat stroke > First aid
conditions: Heat exposure and altered mental status
support: Heat illness may be life-threatening. Seek emergency care for suspected heat stroke and start cooling promptly.
limitations: Delays in active cooling worsen neurologic outcomes.
conflicts: None; aligns with CDC-HEAT.
editorial_note: Core heat-emergency escalation rule.

locator: If you get lost or hurt; call for help
conditions: Outdoor US emergency
support: Communicate location, last known point, situation and needs. Stay put when unable to establish a safe route unless immediate danger requires movement.
limitations: Cell signal is unreliable in backcountry terrain; pre-trip plans bridge communication gaps.
conflicts: None; core lost-person decision rule.
editorial_note: Foundation for stay/signal/move and dispatch handoff cards.

locator: How to stay safe when a flood threatens; take an active role
conditions: U.S. household flood preparedness and evacuation
support: Prepare contacts, medication and supplies. Heed evacuation instructions and avoid flooded roads.
limitations: Six inches of moving water can knock down an adult; shallow-looking crossings hide road washouts.
conflicts: None; aligns with NWS-FLOOD.
editorial_note: Supports flood turnaround and evacuation decision thresholds.

locator: Definition and bearing conversion
conditions: Trip planning with a map and compass
support: Declination varies by date and geographic position. Determine the map reference and current local value.
limitations: Outdated map margins can have meaningful declination drift over decades.
conflicts: None; retained for navigation reconstructions.
editorial_note: Preserved for Z11 continuity.

locator: Heat stroke > Symptoms and First aid
conditions: Suspected heat stroke after exertion or heat exposure
support: Confusion, slurred speech or loss of consciousness can indicate heat stroke. Call 911 and cool the person promptly.
limitations: Exertional heat stroke can occur even in moderate ambient temperatures during heavy effort.
conflicts: None; aligns with T05.
editorial_note: Triggers immediate emergency call and cooling stop condition.

locator: People with Disabilities > Make a Plan and Build a Kit
conditions: Individuals with mobility, sensory, medical, or power-dependent access and functional needs
support: Build a personal support network, plan accessible evacuation transport, register voluntarily with local emergency registries where available, and plan backup power and spare supplies for medical devices, medications, and service animals.
limitations: Local registry availability and utility priority-restoration policies vary by jurisdiction.
conflicts: None; extends generic preparedness plans to accessible requirements.
editorial_note: Directly addresses Z01 accessible emergency planning requirement.
reviewer: Accessible emergency management and disability preparedness

locator: Make a Plan > Family Emergency Communication Plan
conditions: Households and traveling groups preparing for disruptions
support: Record out-of-area contacts, local meeting places, medical/allergy summaries, and alternate communication channels (text vs voice) in paper and offline formats; practice the plan periodically.
limitations: Cellular networks often congest during disasters while SMS or out-of-area contacts may still connect.
conflicts: None; complements outdoor trip-plan cards.
editorial_note: Anchors emergency communication protocols and group contingency plans.

locator: Build a Kit > Basic Disaster Supplies Kit and Maintenance
conditions: Overnight and multi-day emergency readiness
support: Assemble water, food, light, NOAA/battery radio, first aid, whistle, local maps, sanitation, medications, and backup power; inspect expiration dates and batteries regularly.
limitations: Standard 72-hour kits do not cover extended multi-day isolation without replenishment or specialized cold/medical items.
conflicts: None; links kit readiness to periodic maintenance checks.
editorial_note: Supports equipment readiness, inspection, and overnight-emergency cards.

locator: Evacuation > Before, During, and After Evacuation
conditions: Developing wildfire, flood, storm, or infrastructure emergency
support: Identify multiple exit routes ahead of time, keep essential go-bags and fuel ready, leave promptly when authorities order evacuation, and do not return until officials declare the area safe.
limitations: Late departure can trap groups behind road closures, smoke, or rising water.
conflicts: None; pairs with NWS-FLOOD and READY-WILDFIRE.
editorial_note: Establishes clear leave-early decision thresholds for multi-hazard scenarios.

locator: Emergency Alerts > WEA, EAS, and NOAA Weather Radio
conditions: Receiving time-critical hazard warnings at home or outdoors
support: Use multiple redundant alert channels—Wireless Emergency Alerts, local opt-in alerts, and battery/crank NOAA Weather Radio—so a single dead phone or tower outage does not eliminate warning reception.
limitations: Backcountry terrain can block both cellular and VHF weather radio reception.
conflicts: None; aligns with NOAA-NWR.
editorial_note: Grounds emergency warning redundancy in Z01 communication cards.

locator: NOAA Weather Radio All Hazards > Coverage and Receivers
conditions: Weather and civil-hazard monitoring across the United States
support: NOAA Weather Radio broadcasts continuous official warnings directly from NWS offices on VHF frequencies; battery or hand-crank receivers with SAME alerting operate independently of cellular networks.
limitations: VHF line-of-sight range can be attenuated in deep valleys or dense metal structures; verify local transmitter reception before relying on it.
conflicts: None; aligns with READY-ALERTS.
editorial_note: Documents offline weather-alert radio capabilities and reception limits.

locator: Flood Watches and Warnings; Turn Around Don’t Drown
conditions: U.S. flood alerts and routes crossing moving or standing floodwater
support: Use the local flood alert wording and follow directions to move to safer higher ground. Never drive around a barricade or enter a flooded route.
limitations: Stages, timing and detours depend on event and locality; no observable safe crossing depth.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Clarifies Watch vs Warning decision thresholds in Z01 scenarios.

locator: Clean and Separate
conditions: Food preparation with safe water and surfaces
support: Wash hands and separate raw animal foods and juices from ready-to-eat food.
limitations: Requires safe water or approved hand hygiene substitutes in outages.
conflicts: None; retained for food safety pack completeness.
editorial_note: Maintains five-pack integrity.

locator: Cook > Minimum internal temperature
conditions: Food preparation with a working food thermometer
support: Use food-specific safe internal temperatures; visual appearance alone cannot verify cooking.
limitations: Thermometer calibration and probe placement affect readings.
conflicts: None; retained for food safety pack completeness.
editorial_note: Maintains five-pack integrity.

locator: Chill > Refrigerate promptly
conditions: Perishable food outside temperature control
support: Refrigerate within two hours, or within one hour above 90°F.
limitations: Ambient temperature spikes shorten safe holding windows.
conflicts: None; retained for food safety pack completeness.
editorial_note: Maintains five-pack integrity.

locator: Refrigerated food and power outages
conditions: Refrigerator starts cold; keep door closed
support: An unopened refrigerator keeps food cold for about four hours. Follow the per-item discard chart after loss of temperature control. Never taste to test.
limitations: Door openings accelerate warming; appliance thermometer is needed to verify temperature.
conflicts: None; retained for Z15 reconstruction.
editorial_note: Maintains five-pack integrity.

locator: Frozen food and power outages
conditions: Freezer door closed; typical household unit
support: A full freezer holds temperature about 48 hours, a half-full freezer about 24. Use ice crystals or measured 40°F or below to evaluate refreezing where the chart permits.
limitations: Varies by freezer insulation, ambient room temperature, and door seals.
conflicts: None; retained for Z15 reconstruction.
editorial_note: Maintains five-pack integrity.

locator: Ensuring safe canned foods > Acidity and processing methods
conditions: Tested home-canning recipe and equipment
support: Low-acid foods require an applicable tested pressure-canning process; acid foods use the tested process for that recipe.
limitations: Untested modifications can permit Clostridium botulinum survival.
conflicts: None; retained for Z14 reconstruction.
editorial_note: Maintains five-pack integrity.

locator: Ensuring safe canned foods > Altitude effects
conditions: Tested recipe at the actual processing elevation
support: Adjust processing according to the recipe and altitude tables. A change of ingredient or jar size needs a tested recipe that covers it.
limitations: Dial-gauge pressure canners require periodic accuracy testing.
conflicts: None; retained for Z14 reconstruction.
editorial_note: Maintains five-pack integrity.

locator: Hand Tools > General Safety Rules
conditions: Use of knives, saws, axes, hammers and hand tools
support: Keep hand tools in good condition, use the right tool for the job, examine each tool for damage before use, operate according to instructions and wear appropriate personal protective equipment.
limitations: General occupational rules do not replace task-specific forestry or field-tool training.
conflicts: None; baseline tool safety framework.
editorial_note: Anchors tool selection, pre-use inspection and operating boundary cards in Z09.

locator: Hand Tools > Knives, Chisels, Impact and Wrenches
conditions: Manual cutting, striking and prying operations
support: Direct cutting blades away from the body and bystanders, never use cracked wooden handles or mushroomed striking heads, and do not substitute wrenches or blades as pry bars.
limitations: Does not specify material tensile ratings for improvised handles.
conflicts: None; directly informs safe cutting and impact-tool failure cards.
editorial_note: Prevents blade slip, splintered-handle and spalling-metal injuries.

locator: Tool Selection, Inspection and Safe Transport
conditions: Trail and campsite hand tools (axes, saws, shovels, pulaskis, wedges)
support: Inspect handles for splits, loose heads and secure wedges before every use; sheath sharp edges during carry and maintain a clear work circle around swinging tools.
limitations: Forestry guidelines apply to maintained commercial tools; improvised stone or salvaged blades carry higher failure risk.
conflicts: None; aligns with OSHA-3080.
editorial_note: Grounds woodworking, swinging-tool clearance, carrying and maintenance cards.
reviewer: Forestry tool safety and trail maintenance

locator: Sharpening, Filing and Handle Maintenance
conditions: Maintaining cutting edges and wood tool handles in field or shop
support: Secure the tool firmly before filing or honing, keep fingers behind file guards, preserve factory bevel geometry without overheating steel and replace loose or cracked handles rather than taping them.
limitations: Field touch-up honing does not correct chipped, cracked or heat-annealed steel blades.
conflicts: None; separates routine edge maintenance from unsafe handle patching.
editorial_note: Guides sharpening, rust prevention and handle-failure retirement cards.

locator: Sawing, Splitting and Lever Principles
conditions: Cutting downed wood, clearing deadfall and moving heavy logs safely
support: Assess bind and tension in fallen logs before cutting so saws do not pinch or limbs spring back; use solid levers and fulcrums safely without standing in the recoil path of strained timber.
limitations: Complex storm-damaged or hung-up trees require professional sawyers and are outside camp tool scope.
conflicts: None; informs spring-pole, saw-bind and lever mechanical-advantage cards.
editorial_note: Prevents kickback, saw pinching and recoil injuries in Z09.
reviewer: Forestry tool safety and mechanical safety

locator: Forces and Tools > Simple Machines and Mechanical Advantage
conditions: Levers, wedges, inclined planes and friction mechanisms
support: Simple machines trade force for distance (levers, wedges, pulleys); friction, alignment and material strength limit real-world output below ideal ratios.
limitations: Ideal mechanical advantage ignores friction losses and breaking strength of ropes or anchors.
conflicts: None; clarifies physical trade-offs without implying engineered load ratings.
editorial_note: Anchors mechanical-advantage, wedge-splitting and pulley/rigging limit cards.

locator: Repair Kit and Tools
conditions: Field equipment repair during backcountry travel
support: Carry a route-appropriate repair kit (duct/gear tape, multi-tool, cordage, patch supplies) matched to shelter, pack, stove and water gear; verify compatibility before departure.
limitations: Field patches restore temporary function and do not restore full original storm or load ratings.
conflicts: None; aligns with E02 and E20.
editorial_note: Grounds field-repair kits, temporary patches and equipment failure limits.

locator: Personal Protective Equipment and Work Area Control
conditions: Cutting, splitting, striking and rigging operations
support: Maintain stable footing, eye and hand protection appropriate to flying chips or snapped cordage, and clear bystanders outside the swing or snap-back zone.
limitations: Field kits often lack shop PPE, requiring slower conservative technique and lower-energy methods.
conflicts: None; drives snap-back and work-circle exclusion zones in Z09.
editorial_note: Enforces conservative work circles and snap-back clearance.

locator: Cordage, Anchors and Rigging Boundaries
conditions: Non-life-safety camp lashing, tarps, haul lines and tie-downs
support: Cordage strength drops significantly at knots, sharp bends, wet fibers, UV exposure and abrasion; inspect fibers before loading and never use unrated camp cord or improvised bindings for life-safety suspension or climbing.
limitations: No universal breaking strength applies to natural plant fibers or weathered salvaged rope.
conflicts: Counters folklore claims equating improvised cordage to rated climbing rope.
editorial_note: Separates camp utility lashing/hauling from life-safety rigging.

locator: Felling and Overhead Timber Exclusions
conditions: Camp wood preparation and trail clearing
support: Do not fell standing trees or work beneath hung-up limbs without specialized training and gear; restrict routine camp woodworking to small sound downed deadwood where lawful.
limitations: Standing dead trees (snags) fail unpredictably under vibration or wedging.
conflicts: Aligns with E13 and C17.
editorial_note: Reinforces strict downed-wood-only woodworking boundary.

locator: Principle 2 and 5 > Low-Impact Construction and Material Use
conditions: Temporary camp craft and emergency construction on public lands
support: Avoid cutting live saplings, nailing into live trees or building permanent structures on public lands; dismantle temporary non-destructive lashings and leave natural features intact.
limitations: Life-safety emergencies differ from routine camp practice but still require hazard-free builds.
conflicts: Restricts destructive bushcraft construction in routine recreation.
editorial_note: Distinguishes lawful low-impact knots/lashings from destructive camp building.

locator: Wedges, Chisels and Striking Surfaces
conditions: Splitting deadwood or driving stakes with hand tools
support: Avoid steel-on-steel striking of hardened axe polls or unguarded wedges that can chip metal shards; use wooden mallets or purpose-designed striking faces and retire mushroomed heads.
limitations: Improvised stone hammers fracture unpredictably and throw sharp flakes.
conflicts: None; informs baton/wedge/mallet safety cards.
editorial_note: Guides safe splitting, stake driving and struck-tool failure recognition.

locator: US Topo Maps > Coordinate Grids, Scale and Currency
conditions: Map reading and trip planning in the United States
support: USGS topographic maps provide elevation contours, hydrography, roads, land cover and scale/date metadata; check publication date because trails, roads and structures change over time.
limitations: Historical topo sheets (such as 1965 Ely quadrangle) illustrate symbols only and never establish current routes or declination.
conflicts: None; aligns with USGS-MAP-R and NOAA-D.
editorial_note: Grounds map margin, scale, date and historical-excerpt limits in Z11.

locator: Topographic Map Symbols > Contours, Water, Vegetation and Boundaries
conditions: Interpreting standard USGS 1:24,000 and US Topo map sheets
support: Contour spacing indicates slope steepness, index contours give elevation values, blue features mark water/wetlands and standard symbols distinguish roads, trails, cliffs and marshes.
limitations: Small terrain hazards (boulders, undercut banks, fallen timber, thin ice) fall below map contour interval resolution.
conflicts: None; anchors terrain and contour interpretation cards.
editorial_note: Explains contour reading alongside map-resolution limitations.

locator: What is a Topographic Map > Contours and Relief
conditions: Matching three-dimensional terrain shapes to two-dimensional contour lines
support: Closed contour rings denote peaks or depressions (hachured), V-patterns point uphill in valleys/drainages and wide spacing marks gentle slopes while tight spacing marks cliffs or steep grades.
limitations: Dense forest canopy or snow drifts can obscure subtle terrain features shown on the map.
conflicts: None; core topographic terrain-association evidence.
editorial_note: Supports ridge, valley, saddle and handrail terrain-interpretation cards.

locator: Public Domain Status of USGS Topographic Maps
conditions: Reproducing authentic USGS historical/current map excerpts for instruction
support: USGS topographic maps are U.S. government works in the public domain; credit USGS, sheet name, scale, date and map ID clearly and state whether a historical sheet is for symbol study only.
limitations: Commercial map overlays or private trail layers on top of USGS bases may carry separate copyright.
conflicts: None; governs Ely 1965 map excerpt attribution in Z11.
editorial_note: Ensures compliant map provenance and explicit historical-date cautions.

locator: Emergency beacon types and registration
conditions: Emergency satellite distress signaling (406 MHz PLBs and EPIRBs)
support: A 406 MHz distress beacon transmits into the Cospas-Sarsat system. Verify country code, registration and model capabilities separately.
limitations: PLBs are one-way distress alerts only (no two-way texting), require clear sky view and must be reserved for grave and imminent danger.
conflicts: Distinguishes one-way 406 MHz PLBs from commercial two-way satellite messengers.
editorial_note: Anchors beacon selection, sky-view limits and registration cards in Z11.
reviewer: Search and rescue and emergency communications

locator: JetStream > Clouds, Fronts and Atmospheric Pressure
conditions: Field weather observation and short-term storm anticipation
support: Thickening high-to-low cloud decks, rapid barometric drops, towering cumulus building into anvils and backing/shifting winds often signal approaching frontal systems or convective storms.
limitations: Local visual weather signs supplement—and never replace—official NWS forecasts and active warnings.
conflicts: None; separates physical weather cues from folklore sayings.
editorial_note: Grounds cloud, front, wind-shift and microclimate weather cards in Z11.

locator: Fog Safety > Visibility Loss and Travel Hazards
conditions: Dense fog, valley mist, sea fog and blowing-snow whiteout
support: Fog and whiteout collapse visual landmarks and depth perception rapidly, causing disorientation and unintentional terrain/traffic hazards; halt exposed travel early and rely on verified checkpoints or stay put.
limitations: Compass bearings alone cannot reveal hidden cliffs, thin ice or drop-offs in zero visibility.
conflicts: Aligns with B014-P11 whiteout guidance.
editorial_note: Supports whiteout/fog stop thresholds and short-leg navigation boundaries.

locator: NOAA Magnetic Declination > definition and true-bearing conversion
conditions: Using magnetic baseplate compasses near metal, electronics or iron-rich rock
support: Declination is between true and magnetic north and varies by location and time. Grid convergence is separate. A device may already apply a correction.
limitations: NOAA definition does not establish site-specific interference distances or diagnosis of magnetic anomalies.
conflicts: Aligns with B014-P13 and B014-P14.
editorial_note: Grounds declination conversion, metal-clearance and magnetic-anomaly cards.

locator: If You Get Lost; Seek help
conditions: Lost hiker who cannot safely retrace steps and has sought rescue
support: Report last known location and landmarks. Stay put while awaiting help unless an immediate threat requires getting to safety.
limitations: Navigation, signaling method and safe movement depend on site and responder instructions.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Core evidence for lost-person psychology, signaling and SAR coordination cards.

locator: Turn Around Don't Drown > Flooded Crossings and Terrain Detours
conditions: Navigating around flooded streams, washes and submerged roads
support: Water barriers and flooded crossings conceal washed-out banks, swift undercurrents and deep holes; detour along verified dry high-ground routes or hold in a safe elevated spot.
limitations: Applies equally to foot and vehicle navigation.
conflicts: Aligns with B014-P12 and T07.
editorial_note: Connects navigation rerouting to flood and water-barrier boundaries.
reviewer: Search and rescue and emergency management

locator: General Ice Thickness Guidelines > New Clear Ice Only
conditions: Minnesota lakes and ponds during stable winter freezing
support: Agency thickness guidelines apply ONLY to new, clear solid ice and are NEVER a guarantee of safety; white snow-ice is roughly half as strong, and currents, springs, inlets, outlets and snow cover create hidden thin zones.
limitations: No ice is 100% safe; one drilled thickness check does not clear an entire crossing route.
conflicts: Directly reconciles B013 P01–P05, P11 and P17 with MN DNR warnings.
editorial_note: Enforces non-guarantee ice boundaries across Z12.
reviewer: Ice safety and winter search and rescue

locator: Cold Water Safety > Cold Shock, Swim Failure and Hypothermia
conditions: Immersion in water below 70°F (especially below 50°F / winter ice water)
support: Cold shock can cause involuntary gasping and rapid breathing. Grip and swimming may deteriorate rapidly; flotation and early rescue matter. Onset and severity vary.
limitations: Strong swimmers drown rapidly from cold shock and muscle incapacitation without flotation.
conflicts: Refutes myth that hypothermia is the only immediate cold-water killer.
editorial_note: Core physiological evidence for Z12 ice-breakthrough and maritime immersion cards.

locator: Cold Water Hazards > 1-10-1 Principle and Survival Actions
conditions: Unexpected immersion in cold lakes, rivers, coastal or marine waters
support: Protect the airway, use flotation, get out safely if possible, and prioritize rescue. The 1-10-1 mnemonic is descriptive and does not establish deadlines or survival times.
limitations: Exact individual survival minutes vary widely with body size, clothing, sea state and water temperature.
conflicts: None; aligns with MN-COLDW and USCG guidance.
editorial_note: Anchors cold-water immersion decision thresholds in Z12.

locator: Wearing Your Life Jacket > Fit, Flotation and Cold Water
conditions: Boating, paddling, coastal craft and icy-shoreline marine operations
support: Wear a correctly fitted, fastened U.S. Coast Guard-approved life jacket suited to activity and wearer. Flotation reduces risk but does not guarantee airway position, especially when unconscious.
limitations: Inflatable PFDs require arming inspection and are unsuitable for high-impact whitewater or non-swimmers per label.
conflicts: None; aligns with USCG-SAFE.
editorial_note: Grounds PFD readiness and maritime abandonment cards in Z12.
reviewer: Maritime safety and search and rescue

locator: Boating Safety > Float Plans, VHF-DSC, Weather and Abandon-Ship Limits
conditions: Inland large lakes, coastal waters and maritime travel
support: File a float plan, monitor marine weather and VHF Channel 16/DSC where equipped, stay with a swamped buoyant hull when safer than swimming to distant shore and maintain visual/electronic distress signals.
limitations: Open-water craft operations require vessel-specific seamanship beyond general survival cards.
conflicts: None; aligns with NOAA-MARINE and NOAA-SARSAT.
editorial_note: Anchors maritime communication, hull-stay and distress cards in Z12.

locator: Marine Weather Services > Small Craft Advisories, Gale Warnings and Sea State
conditions: Coastal, Great Lakes and open-water marine zones
support: Marine forecasts issue Small Craft Advisories, Gale, Storm and Hazardous Seas Warnings; wind opposing tide or shallow shoals steepens breaking waves dramatically faster than inland forecasts indicate.
limitations: Local fetch and headland funneling can exceed regional zone forecasts.
conflicts: None; integrates with NOAA-NWR marine channels.
editorial_note: Guides marine weather thresholds and coastal-craft abort cards in Z12.

locator: Death Valley Safety > Desert Heat, Dehydration, Flash Floods and Vehicle Breakdown
conditions: Arid desert travel, canyon country and extreme summer heat
support: Desert heat accelerates fluid and electrolyte loss rapidly, temperatures inside parked vehicles spike to fatal levels within minutes, dry washes flash-flood from distant storms and staying with a disabled road vehicle is generally safer than walking into extreme heat.
limitations: Cell service is widely absent across desert basins; water needs can exceed 1 gallon/day dramatically during heat.
conflicts: None; aligns with CDC-HEAT and NWS-HEAT.
editorial_note: Core desert-environment evidence across Z12 heat/arid cards.

locator: Drought Safety > Dry Soils, Dust Storms and Extreme Fire Risk
conditions: Arid regions, seasonal drought and dry-basin travel
support: Drought dries seasonal springs, hardens soils so sudden rain runs off instantly into flash floods, raises wildfire intensity and produces blinding dust storms (haboobs) where drivers must pull completely off roadways with lights off.
limitations: Flash-flood risk rises paradoxically on parched hydrophobic desert ground.
conflicts: None; complements NPS-DESERT and NWS-WILDFIRE.
editorial_note: Grounds desert flash-flood, dust-storm and dry-source cards in Z12.

locator: Travel to High Altitudes > Acclimatization, AMS, HAPE and HACE
conditions: Mountain travel above ~8,000 feet (2,500 meters)
support: Ascend gradually to acclimatize; recognize Acute Mountain Sickness (headache, nausea, fatigue) and life-threatening HAPE (shortness of breath at rest, cough) or HACE (ataxia, confusion), for which immediate descent and medical care are essential.
limitations: Physical fitness does not prevent altitude illness; individual susceptibility varies unpredictably.
conflicts: None; aligns with NPS-MTN.
editorial_note: Core physiological evidence for Z12 mountain-altitude cards.

locator: Annual Climate Conditions; seasonal descriptions
conditions: High-elevation ridges, alpine passes and mountain weather
support: Mountain temperatures drop sharply with elevation and sunset, afternoon thunderstorms build rapidly over exposed ridges (requiring early starts and turning back below treeline), and steep snowfields conceal runout hazards.
limitations: Clear morning skies routinely shift to severe lightning and sleet by early afternoon.
conflicts: None; integrates with E07, E23 and CDC-ALT.
editorial_note: Grounds mountain timing, treeline retreat and elevation-cooling cards.

locator: Landslides and Debris Flow > Warning Signs and Burn Scars
conditions: Steep slopes, recent wildfire burn scars and saturated mountain/coastal terrain
support: Heavy rainfall on steep terrain or wildfire burn scars triggers fast-moving debris flows; watch for rumbling, tilting trees, sudden muddy stream surges or new ground cracks and evacuate perpendicular/uphill away from valleys immediately.
limitations: Debris flows travel faster than a person can run and recur in previously scarred drainages.
conflicts: None; pairs with E04 and E17.
editorial_note: Supports mountain/burn-scar landslide and debris-flow hazard cards.

locator: What is a Wetland > Bogs, Fens, Swamps and Marshes
conditions: Upper Midwest boreal bogs, marshes, beaver ponds and coastal wetlands
support: Wetlands feature saturated hydric soils, floating vegetation mats (quaking bogs), hidden channels and fluctuating water tables that conceal deep muck, unstable footing and slow-draining floodwaters.
limitations: Winter ice over bogs and wetlands is especially erratic due to decaying organic heat and seepage.
conflicts: Aligns with B014-P12 and NPS-WETLAND.
editorial_note: Core wetland terrain and quaking-bog hazard evidence in Z12.
reviewer: Wetland ecology and search and rescue

locator: Wetlands > Footing, Immersion, Insects and Water Quality
conditions: Travel near marshes, swamps, fens and slow-water estuaries
support: Wetlands combine wet-cold immersion risk, concealed snags, unstable muck that drains energy rapidly, insect-borne disease exposure and high-organic/stagnant water requiring strict treatment or alternate sourcing.
limitations: Footwear immersion and trench-foot/cold injury occur even in mild temperatures during prolonged wetland exposure.
conflicts: None; complements EPA-WETLAND and W16.
editorial_note: Grounds wetland navigation, foot-care and cold-wet exposure cards.

locator: How to escape a rip current
conditions: Caught in a rip current on a surf beach
support: Do not fight the current. Float or tread water and signal for help. Swim out across the flow only if able and conditions permit.
limitations: The current, shoreline, flotation and ability vary. A universal escape direction and visual diagnosis are unsafe.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Core coastal surf and Great Lakes rip-current card evidence.

locator: What are Tides? · tidal range and tidal current
conditions: Ocean coastlines, sea caves, tidal flats and rocky headlands
support: Tidal height and tidal current describe different properties. Rising or falling water may be accompanied by horizontal flow.
limitations: Local timing and accessible routes require the actual site forecast and observations. Do not infer a safe route from a general tide stage.
conflicts: None; pairs with NOAA-COAST.
editorial_note: Grounds tidal-cutoff, headland and mudflat planning cards in Z12.

locator: Tsunami Safety > Natural Warning Signs and Immediate High-Ground Evacuation
conditions: Earthquake-prone ocean coastlines and coastal estuaries
support: Strong or long coastal ground shaking, a loud ocean roar or sudden unusual ocean recession are natural tsunami warnings—move immediately on foot inland and to high ground without waiting for official sirens, and stay away until officials issue an all-clear (multiple waves arrive over hours).
limitations: A first receding or modest wave is often followed by much larger destructive surges.
conflicts: None; aligns with READY-TSUNAMI.
editorial_note: Establishes coastal tsunami immediate-evacuation stop conditions.

locator: Hurricane Safety > Storm Surge, Coastal Flooding and Inland Wind
conditions: Tropical storms and hurricanes impacting coastal and near-coastal zones
support: Storm surge and inland rainfall flooding are the deadliest hurricane hazards; obey coastal evacuation orders early, never shelter in low coastal zones or boats and treat calm storm eyes as temporary pauses before violent winds reverse.
limitations: Hazardous rip currents and swell arrive hundreds of miles ahead of landfall.
conflicts: None; aligns with READY-EVAC and T13.
editorial_note: Grounds coastal storm-surge and hurricane evacuation cards in Z12.

locator: Self-rescue after falling in
conditions: Cold-water ice breakthrough on frozen lakes or rivers
support: Face the direction you came from if able, regain breathing control, kick and use the edge or picks, and remain low after exit. Prior support is not guaranteed safe ice.
limitations: Ice rescue carries extreme drowning risk for untrained rescuers; dry practice and qualified rescue review are mandatory.
conflicts: Directly aligns with B013 P06–P08 and P14; carries high-consequence specialist review hold.
editorial_note: Anchored in Z12 ice-breakthrough cards and logged in the Astra escalation register.
reviewer: Ice rescue, EMS and wilderness medicine

locator: DANGER > Fire and explosion; Stove set-up
conditions: PocketRocket 2 or its exact replacement instructions
support: The PocketRocket 2 manual prohibits windscreens and specifies safe outdoor use, clearances and handling.
limitations: Model-specific. Other equipment requires its own current instructions.
conflicts: See A01 cross-zone review.
editorial_note: Use only within the stated conditions.

locator: Simple machines; independent A01 static force-balance derivation
conditions: Unloaded schematic of an ideal fixed redirect; two equal line tensions
support: The force on the redirect is the vector sum of the two rope pulls. Equal tensions T give 2T for parallel pulls in the same direction and square-root-of-two times T for perpendicular directions.
limitations: Independent statics derivation, not a numerical lifting limit. Friction, shock and support geometry invalidate simplified assumptions.
conflicts: See A01 cross-zone review.
editorial_note: Use only within the stated conditions.

locator: US Topo map metadata; map collar
conditions: Consumer map and receiver; exact horizontal datum and coordinate format
support: Check the horizontal reference and coordinate format before plotting. Do not assume mixed datums identify the same point.
limitations: Datum transformation is location- and frame-dependent; use authoritative conversion.
conflicts: See A01 cross-zone review.
editorial_note: Use only within the stated conditions.

locator: Registration, renewal and accidental activation
conditions: U.S.-coded 406 MHz emergency beacons
support: Register and verify information every two years. Report false activation to the appropriate rescue coordination center with beacon details.
limitations: Equipment and national authority vary; use the current beacon and NOAA instructions.
conflicts: See A01 cross-zone review.
editorial_note: Use only within the stated conditions.

locator: Visitor protection > Search and rescue
conditions: People waiting for organized air rescue
support: Remain clear and follow explicit directions from the flight crew or dispatch.
limitations: Conservative editorial boundary. Agency program page does not supply a layman landing-zone or approach procedure.
conflicts: See A01 cross-zone review.
editorial_note: Use only within the stated conditions.

locator: Self-rescue steps after falling through
conditions: Person already immersed after ice failure
support: If able, face the approach route, regain breathing control, kick and pull out, and remain low to the surface after exiting.
limitations: Prior route is not a strength guarantee; no timed window or operational qualification.
conflicts: See A01 cross-zone review.
editorial_note: Use only within the stated conditions.

locator: Call 911; Reach and Throw
conditions: Untrained witness on stable shore
support: Call 911. Offer assistance from safe shore only and release a reach object if it begins pulling you in.
limitations: The draft lay boundary excludes going onto ice.
conflicts: See A01 cross-zone review.
editorial_note: Use only within the stated conditions.

locator: What to do if caught in a rip current
conditions: Swimmer in surf with seaward rip flow
support: Avoid fighting the current. Float or tread and signal. If able, exit out of the current along shore and then return toward safety.
limitations: Shore shape, flow and swimming ability vary; no guaranteed escape geometry.
conflicts: See A01 cross-zone review.
editorial_note: Use only within the stated conditions.

locator: Why sneaker waves are dangerous and beach precautions
conditions: Coast exposed to breaking swell and mobile logs
support: A higher wave can follow a quiet interval and reach beyond prior waves. Stay back and heed local warnings.
limitations: No fixed number of waves or minutes establishes safety.
conflicts: See A01 cross-zone review.
editorial_note: Use only within the stated conditions.

locator: Identify evacuation routes and safe locations
conditions: Coastal tsunami evacuation planning
support: Use local tsunami zones, evacuation routes and designated high ground.
limitations: Fallback advice does not replace local warning or accessibility plans.
