conflicts: See A01 cross-zone review.
editorial_note: Use only within the stated conditions.

locator: Ensure Your Own Safety; Find Life-Threatening Bleeding; Compress
conditions: Lay responder encountering severe external hemorrhage
support: Ensure scene safety first, call 911, expose the wound to locate life-threatening bleeding, and apply firm continuous direct pressure with clean gauze or cloth.
limitations: Does not replace formal hands-on Stop the Bleed training or EMS trauma care.
conflicts: None across ACS/ARC guidelines.
editorial_note: Separates life-threatening arterial/venous hemorrhage from minor scrapes.

locator: How to Apply a Tourniquet; Windlass Rod Tourniquet
conditions: Life-threatening extremity bleeding, visible wound, suitable commercial device
support: Place the device 2–3 inches toward the torso from the wound, between wound and heart, clear of joints. Tighten until bleeding stops and leave in place for medical personnel.
limitations: Identify a visible wound and follow the exact device and training. This is not the tactical high-and-tight rule or a pediatric device-fit approval.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Governs extremity hemorrhage escalation and strict EMS handoff documentation.

locator: Figure 2 Adult Basic Life Support Algorithm for Lay Rescuers; 6.1 Recognition of Cardiac Arrest
conditions: Unresponsive adult with absent or abnormal breathing; early dispatch and AED access
support: Recognize gasps as abnormal, activate EMS, start CPR and use an AED promptly. Follow prompts and resume after analysis or shock.
limitations: Pediatric and drowning arrest require their own training or dispatch prompts; the adult cardiac-arrest algorithm is not all-age guidance.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Distinguishes lay activation and dispatcher-guided CPR from advanced life support.

locator: 10 Adult Foreign-Body Airway Obstruction, sections 10.1–10.3
conditions: Responsive adults with mild or severe airway obstruction; separate unresponsive branch
support: Watch an effective cough. Activate EMS for severe signs and provide trained or dispatcher-directed care. Begin CPR when unresponsive and avoid blind finger sweeps.
limitations: Infants and children require the pediatric protocol. Pregnancy and inability to encircle the abdomen change thrust technique.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Keeps airway maneuvers bounded by formal training and 911 dispatcher guidance.

locator: Recognizing Circulatory Shock and Positioning
conditions: Injured or ill patient with pale cool clammy skin, rapid weak pulse, confusion, or dizziness
support: Treat suspected shock as a life-threatening emergency: call 911, control external bleeding, keep the person warm and insulated from cold ground, and do not give food or drink.
limitations: Field responders cannot diagnose internal hemorrhage or administer IV fluids.
conflicts: None; reinforces keeping suspected shock patients NPO and warm.
editorial_note: Core shock recognition and stabilization boundary in Z10.

locator: Minor Wound Cleaning, Protection, and Infection Red Flags
conditions: Superficial cuts, scrapes, and abrasions with potable water available
support: Rinse minor wounds thoroughly with clean potable water, cover with a clean sterile dressing, and monitor for worsening redness, warmth, swelling, pus, red streaks, or fever.
limitations: Deep punctures, animal bites, retained foreign bodies, or heavily contaminated wounds require clinical evaluation and tetanus review.
conflicts: None; separates clean potable rinsing from harsh chemical wound scrubbing.
editorial_note: Anchors field wound hygiene and infection escalation cards.

locator: Thermal Burn Cooling, Covering, and Severity Escalation
conditions: Minor vs major thermal burns (flame, scald, contact)
support: Cool minor superficial burns with cool (not icy) running water, remove constricting rings/clothing not stuck to skin, cover loosely with clean non-stick dressing, and seek emergency care for deep, large, facial, hand, foot, genital, joint, or airway burns.
limitations: Never apply ice, butter, grease, or ointments to fresh burns, and do not pop intact blisters.
conflicts: None; aligns with ARC/ABA lay burn first aid.
editorial_note: Establishes burn-cooling limits and automatic clinical-escalation zones.

locator: Anaphylaxis
conditions: Suspected severe allergic reaction; community first aid; prescribed epinephrine or applicable local protocol
support: Activate EMS promptly and assist with epinephrine under the relevant device or action plan. Follow professional direction for subsequent care.
limitations: Pediatric device selection, subsequent dose, timing and transfer require product, patient and local protocol.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Separates assisting with a patient's prescribed auto-injector from lay prescribing.

locator: Suspected Fracture Stabilization and Neurovascular Checks
conditions: Suspected limb fracture, deformity, or inability to bear weight
support: Immobilize the injured limb in the position found using padded support without attempting to straighten visibly deformed bones; check circulation, sensation, and movement beyond the injury and arrange evacuation.
limitations: Open fractures (bone breaking skin) and femur/pelvis injuries carry high bleeding and infection risk requiring urgent EMS.
conflicts: None; forbids lay fracture reduction in routine field care.
editorial_note: Anchors splinting, neurovascular checks, and evacuation urgency in Z10.

locator: Soft-Tissue Sprain/Strain Care and Mobility Decisions
conditions: Ankle, knee, or wrist sprains without deformity or open wound
support: Rest the joint, support with comfortable stabilization, protect from further load, and evaluate whether the patient can safely self-evacuate or requires extraction; persistent inability to bear weight warrants clinical imaging.
limitations: Severe sprains and undisplaced fractures cannot be reliably distinguished without X-ray.
conflicts: None; treats field assessment as functional evacuation triage, not diagnosis.
editorial_note: Prevents walking on unstable fractures under the assumption of a mild sprain.

locator: Danger signs in adults; Danger signs in children
conditions: Head impact or suspected mild brain injury; age matters
support: Seek emergency care for danger signs such as worsening headache, repeated vomiting, altered behavior or difficulty waking.
limitations: Spinal precautions, older-adult blood thinners, and return to activity require separate clinical or dispatcher guidance.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Grounds head-trauma, concussion, and spinal-motion-restriction cards.

locator: Animal Bites, Rabies Exposure, and Wound Infection
conditions: Wild or domestic mammal bites or scratches breaking skin
support: Wash bite wounds promptly with soap and clean running water, control bleeding, and obtain prompt medical evaluation for infection risk, tetanus status, and rabies post-exposure assessment.
limitations: Bat encounters in sleeping areas can cause unrecognized bites requiring public-health rabies consultation.
conflicts: None; aligns with CDC rabies guidance.
editorial_note: Anchors mammal-bite hygiene and public-health rabies referral.

locator: First aid and prohibited actions
conditions: Suspected venomous snakebite in the United States; rescuer safely out of striking range
support: Call EMS and seek emergency treatment. Keep the person still, remove restrictive items, and do not catch the snake or use cutting, suction, ice or a tourniquet.
limitations: Snake guidance does not transfer to arthropod stings, foreign protocols or toxin identification.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Hard-stop non-invasive snakebite and venomous-bite protocol.

locator: How to remove a tick; Symptoms after a tick bite
conditions: Attached tick on a person in U.S. settings
support: Remove promptly with clean fine-tipped tweezers close to the skin and steady upward pressure. Clean the site and obtain evaluation for rash or fever in subsequent weeks.
limitations: No image determines species, prophylaxis or ruling out illness.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Core Upper Midwest vector-borne disease prevention card evidence.
reviewer: Infectious disease and regional public health

locator: First aid for swallowed, inhaled, skin and eye exposure; when to call 911
conditions: Suspected poisoning in the U.S.
support: For collapse, seizure, breathing trouble or inability to wake call 911. Otherwise get timely poison-center advice. Do not induce vomiting.
limitations: Substance and route determine immediate care. Keep rescuers away from contaminated scenes.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Separates 911 life-threat activation from Poison Control guidance.

locator: Get help from poison experts; route-specific first aid
conditions: U.S. poison exposure, when safe to obtain details
support: Give Poison Control the substance, exposure route and symptoms. Follow case-specific instructions.
limitations: Use existing labels or photos from a safe position. Collecting a sample is an editorially excluded action where risk exists.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Guides documentation and anti-folklore poison response in Z10.

locator: Dehydration Recognition, Oral Rehydration, and Red Flags
conditions: Heat exertion, prolonged diarrhea, vomiting, or inadequate water intake
support: Encourage small frequent sips of safe potable water or labeled oral rehydration solution in alert patients able to swallow; evacuate urgently for confusion, inability to keep fluids down, sunken eyes, or minimal dark urine.
limitations: Severely dehydrated or altered patients cannot safely rehydrate by mouth alone.
conflicts: None; avoids unverified homemade salt-sugar ratio guesswork when labeled packets exist.
editorial_note: Links hydration monitoring to medical evacuation triggers.

locator: In the eye: immediate irrigation; after irrigation
conditions: Liquid chemical splash in the eye; exclude embedded or penetrating injury
support: Begin immediate room-temperature water irrigation for at least 15–20 minutes and obtain poison-center direction.
limitations: Severe or persistent symptoms need urgent evaluation. A penetrating injury follows a separate no-pressure emergency care branch; consult ocular trauma guidance.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Core eye-trauma decision boundary in Z10.

locator: Internal Bleeding, Nosebleed, and Dressing Monitoring
conditions: External vs suspected internal hemorrhage and severe epistaxis
support: For routine nosebleed, sit upright leaning slightly forward and pinch the soft part of the nose continuously; escalate urgently for uncontrolled bleeding, coughing/vomiting blood, abdominal rigidity, or dizziness.
limitations: Tilting the head backward causes blood swallowing and airway irritation.
conflicts: None; distinguishes minor nosebleed from internal-bleeding emergencies.
editorial_note: Supports bleeding sub-scenarios and recheck cadence.

locator: Lay First-Aid Scope, Kit Readiness, and Documentation
conditions: Pre-trip kit preparation and remote patient monitoring
support: Maintain an inspected, unexpired first-aid kit matched to your actual training, keep written patient observations (time, responsiveness, breathing, symptoms, interventions) for EMS handoff, and practice skills in certified courses.
limitations: Carrying advanced medical instruments without clinical training adds risk rather than capability.
conflicts: None; aligns with ARC and NPS-K.
editorial_note: Anchors kit sizing, SOAP-style lay observation logs, and scope-of-practice cards.

locator: Blisters, Foot Care, and Skin Integrity in Field Travel
conditions: Friction hot spots and intact vs torn skin blisters during multi-day travel
support: Address friction hot spots early by stopping to adjust socks/footwear and protecting skin with clean padding; keep intact blisters clean and unpopped when practical and watch torn skin closely for infection.
limitations: Patients with diabetes or poor circulation face severe foot-infection risk and require early clinical review.
conflicts: None; emphasizes prevention over invasive blister lancing.
editorial_note: Grounds backcountry foot hygiene and infection prevention.

locator: Positioning of the Ill or Injured Person
conditions: Decreased alertness with normal breathing; no suspected neck/back/hip/pelvis injury
support: Side-lying recovery position can be reasonable; reassess breathing continuously and act if it becomes abnormal.
limitations: Avoid unnecessary movement after suspected spinal or pelvic injury. A recovery position may delay recognition of apnea if unmonitored.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Anchors airway-protection positioning and handoff documentation.

locator: What to do; emergency response
conditions: Suspected hypothermia or cold-related altered alertness
support: Seek emergency help, handle gently, prevent further cooling and warm the body core within training.
limitations: No fixed lay delay before calling or following dispatch on CPR. Separate expert protocols require temperature, pulse and training context.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Links Z10 clinical cold care with Z12 environmental prevention.

locator: Field treatment, avoid refreezing; rapid water-bath rewarming
conditions: Suspected frozen tissue without safe definitive care
support: Protect from refreezing and mechanical injury. Any active rewarming requires the guideline’s conditions and a safe no-refreezing plan.
limitations: Temperature, duration and transfer are clinical decisions; avoid converting the guideline into a universal field recipe.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Core clinical frostbite decision boundary in Z10.

locator: Power Outages > Preparing and Responding Safely
conditions: Residential utility electrical outages of hours to days
support: Keep phones/medical batteries charged, maintain flashlights instead of candles, unplug sensitive appliances to protect against restoration surges, and verify backup power plans for electrically dependent medical devices.
limitations: Home outage durations vary widely by grid damage; extended winter outages require heat/evacuation contingencies.
conflicts: None; aligns with CPSC and NFPA.
editorial_note: Establishes household outage baseline and medical-power priority in Z13.

locator: Use portable generators outdoors; keep exhaust away
conditions: Portable generator during household outage
support: Run outdoors at least 20 feet from buildings and direct exhaust away. Use approved connections as the manual dictates; licensed electrical work governs transfer to a building. Never backfeed.
limitations: Distance alone does not guarantee safety. Local code and exact equipment determine installation.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Core electrical isolation boundary across Z13 generator cards.

locator: Heating Equipment Safety > Space Heaters, Fireplaces, and Clearances
conditions: Residential winter heating and supplemental backup heating
support: Maintain at least a 3-foot clearance between anything flammable and any heating source (space heaters, fireplaces, wood stoves), inspect chimneys annually, use only the fuel specified by the heater manufacturer, and never use kitchen ovens to heat homes.
limitations: Unvented fuel-burning heaters also create severe carbon monoxide and indoor air hazards; local building codes govern installations.
conflicts: None; aligns with CPSC-C and READY-HOME-F.
editorial_note: Grounds safe supplemental heating clearances and stop boundaries in Z13.
reviewer: Fire safety and licensed HVAC trades

locator: Home Fires > Smoke Alarms, Fire Extinguishers, and Escape Plans
conditions: Residential fire prevention during outages and supplemental heating
support: Test smoke alarms monthly on every level and outside sleeping areas, keep two exits clear from every room, store fuels outside living spaces in approved containers, and evacuate immediately if a fire exceeds incipient containment.
limitations: Candles and improvised indoor flames dramatically elevate outage house-fire deaths.
conflicts: None; integrates with CPSC CO-alarm rules (C09).
editorial_note: Anchors outage fire prevention, fuel storage, and exit readiness in Z13.

locator: Private Drinking Water Wells > Maintenance, Floods, and Testing
conditions: Households relying on private domestic groundwater wells
support: Private wells are not regulated by municipal utilities; test water annually (and after any flood, power loss with pressure drop, or plumbing repair) through a certified laboratory and keep wellheads sealed above grade away from runoff and chemicals.
limitations: Visual clarity or normal taste never proves a private well is free of bacteria, nitrates, or arsenic.
conflicts: None; aligns with CDC-WELL (W18) and MDH-WELL-HOME.
editorial_note: Core private-well governance and testing cadence in Z13.
reviewer: Hydrogeology, licensed well contractor, and public health

locator: Wells and Borings > Minnesota Private Well Standards and Disinfection
conditions: Minnesota and Upper Midwest private residential wells
support: Use a licensed Minnesota well contractor for wellhead repair, electrical pump work, or shock disinfection after flooding or backflow; maintain sanitary well caps and isolate well casings from surface snowmelt and agricultural runoff.
limitations: DIY well-cap removal or improper chlorine mixing risks aquifer contamination and electrical shock.
conflicts: None; regionalizes EPA-WELL for Minnesota conditions.
editorial_note: Anchors Upper Midwest private-well resilience and licensed-trade handoff.
reviewer: Minnesota environmental health and licensed well trades

locator: Do I pump my tank during flooded or saturated drainfield conditions?; After the flood
conditions: Flooded or saturated septic drainfield
support: Conserve water and do not pump while the field is flooded or saturated. Arrange professional inspection and qualified servicing as conditions permit.
limitations: Avoid use until local or professional directions allow. Tank buoyancy and recovery depend on site and system.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Grounds septic-system limits and outage water conservation in Z13.
reviewer: Onsite wastewater engineering and public health

locator: Water > Emergency Household Supply, Shutoff, and Alternate Indoor Sources
conditions: Household plumbing disruptions, water-main breaks, or winter freeze outages
support: Store at least 1 gallon per person per day for several days (two weeks where feasible for extended outages), know the main water shutoff valve location, and recognize clean indoor water-heater reserve boundaries only after shutting off power/gas and confirming supply safety.
limitations: Never use water from radiators, hot-water boilers, or chemically treated toilet tanks for drinking.
conflicts: None; complements CDC-S (W06, W14).
editorial_note: Covers household water shutoffs, pipe-freeze prevention, and safe indoor reserves.
reviewer: Plumbing safety and drinking-water public health

locator: Messages to share; lithium-ion battery safety
conditions: Consumer battery charging, storage, use and visible failure
support: Follow manufacturer limits and use certified compatible equipment. Stop use for heat, swelling, noise, leaks or unusual smell. Evacuate and call for help during an active incident.
limitations: Battery electrical protection, flooding, thermal faults and lead-acid installation require applicable specialist review. Do not handle failing cells.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Grounds portable power sizing, inverter limits, and battery fire safety.

locator: Winter Household Resilience > Frozen Pipes, Ice Dams, and Heating Loss
conditions: Sub-zero Upper Midwest winter outages and prolonged cold snaps
support: Prevent burst pipes by insulating exposed lines, keeping cabinet doors open, shutting off and draining water lines per plumbing guidance if indoor temperatures drop toward freezing, and consolidating household occupants into one safe insulated interior room.
limitations: Draining hydronic boilers or gas water heaters requires exact manufacturer/plumber steps to prevent equipment damage or gas leaks.
conflicts: None; regionalizes winter home defense for Minnesota conditions.
editorial_note: Anchors winter pipe protection, thermal-zone consolidation, and abandonment thresholds.
reviewer: Residential plumbing, HVAC, and cold-weather emergency management

locator: What to DO; What Not to Do
conditions: Suspected gas or pipeline leak
support: Leave the affected area and call 911 and the provider from safety. Avoid spark sources and leave valve and restoration decisions to authorized responders.
limitations: Do not transpose outdoor hazmat sheltering directions to a gas leak inside the dwelling.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Establishes strict utility-leak evacuation and licensed restoration gates.
reviewer: Gas utility safety and fire service

locator: Home Alarms > Smoke, Carbon Monoxide, and Battery Backup Readiness
conditions: Occupied residences with fuel-burning furnaces, water heaters, attached garages, or outage generators
support: Maintain interconnected or battery-backed CO and smoke alarms on every floor and outside sleeping rooms, replace expired sensors on schedule, and keep exterior furnace/dryer/exhaust vents clear of drifting snow.
limitations: Blocked high-efficiency PVC furnace intake/exhaust pipes in heavy snow can force CO back indoors or lock out heating systems.
conflicts: None; integrates with C09 and Z13-R03.
editorial_note: Connects winter snow-drift vent inspection to household CO prevention.
reviewer: Carbon monoxide safety and residential HVAC

locator: Sanitation, Hand Hygiene, and Emergency Waste Containment
conditions: Household water-service or sewer interruption
support: Maintain separate handwashing stations using safe water and soap (or alcohol hand rub when hands are not visibly soiled), line emergency bucket toilets with heavy bags and tight lids when sewer service is unusable, and never mix bleach with ammonia or acids.
limitations: Improvised sanitation is a temporary containment bridge until municipal sewer or licensed sanitation resumes; follow local health department disposal orders.
conflicts: None; prevents fecal-oral outbreaks and toxic chloramine gas mixing.
editorial_note: Core household sanitation and chemical-mixing boundary in Z13.

locator: Household Emergency Planning, Utility Maps, and Outage Checklists
conditions: Pre-outage residential documentation and household drills
support: Document main water, electrical panel, and gas shutoff locations, utility outage phone numbers, medical power registries, and neighborhood check-in networks on paper before storms hit.
limitations: Utility medical-priority lists do not guarantee uninterrupted power during major ice storms or grid blackouts.
conflicts: None; bridges Z01 planning with Z13 household infrastructure.
editorial_note: Grounds household utility mapping and vulnerable-occupant contingencies.

locator: Generator fire and carbon monoxide safety; operation and refueling
conditions: Portable generator in open air, manual and site permit its use
support: Keep equipment dry and use manufacturer-permitted protection only if it preserves safe outdoor placement. Refuel with the engine off after cooling.
limitations: No universal canopy or grounding scheme; ask a licensed electrician and keep evacuation ahead of shutdown after possible indoor exhaust exposure.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Covers wet-weather generator enclosures, refueling cooldown, and shock prevention.

locator: Household Emergency Communications During Grid and Cell Outages
conditions: Residential power, internet, and cellular tower disruptions
support: Maintain a battery/crank NOAA Weather Radio, spare power banks, car-charger backups, written contact cards, and local AM/FM broadcast station lists so warnings and utility restoration updates remain accessible without Wi-Fi or cell data.
limitations: Cordless landline handsets and VoIP routers fail immediately when house power drops unless separately backed up.
conflicts: None; links Z13 household comms to Z15 disaster alerts.
editorial_note: Grounds home communications continuity during extended blackouts.

locator: Household Evacuation Thresholds When Utilities Fail
conditions: Uninhabitable indoor temperatures, sewage backup, persistent CO alarm, or structural/utility hazard
support: Establish clear pre-agreed exit triggers to relocate to a warming center, hotel, or relatives BEFORE indoor freezing, carbon monoxide alarms, medical-device battery exhaustion, or impassable blizzard roads trap occupants.
limitations: Waiting until indoor pipes burst or batteries hit zero removes safe travel options.
conflicts: None; aligns with T13 and E14.
editorial_note: Defines objective household abandonment thresholds in Z13.

locator: Wood Stoves, Chimneys, Ash Disposal, and Fuel Storage Safety
conditions: Residences heated by properly installed wood stoves or fireplaces
support: Burn seasoned dry wood only, clean creosote-prone chimneys regularly through qualified sweeps, empty cooled ashes strictly into lidded metal containers set outdoors well away from decks and structures, and never burn treated lumber or trash indoors.
limitations: Embers stay hot enough to ignite cardboard or wood decks days after a fire appears dead.
conflicts: None; critical winter wood-heat fire prevention boundary.
editorial_note: Covers solid-fuel residential heating maintenance and ash-fire failure modes.
reviewer: Fire safety and certified chimney/HVAC trades

locator: Site Selection, Sunlight, Frost Dates, and Short-Season Planning
conditions: Home vegetable gardening in Upper Midwest / Minnesota (USDA Zones 3–5)
support: Select a sunny well-drained garden site receiving 6–8+ hours of direct sunlight, match crop days-to-maturity to local last-spring and first-autumn frost dates, and separate cool-season crops from frost-sensitive warm-season crops.
limitations: Microclimates, low frost pockets, and soil clay/sand composition shift local planting windows by weeks.
conflicts: None; anchors regional Minnesota growing-season realism.
editorial_note: Grounds Z14 regional food production and frost-window planning.

locator: Soil Preparation, Testing, Compost, and Safe Fertility
conditions: Residential garden beds and small-acreage food plots
support: Test garden soil through an accredited lab (e.g., UMN Soil Testing Lab) before heavy amending to determine pH, nutrients, and urban lead risk; incorporate finished compost and avoid applying raw animal manure immediately before harvesting edible crops.
limitations: Urban soils near older painted buildings or roads may contain legacy lead requiring raised beds and clean soil barriers.
conflicts: None; links soil fertility to food-safety contamination prevention.
editorial_note: Separates safe composted soil building from pathogen/heavy-metal hazards.

locator: Watering, Mulching, Crop Rotation, and Integrated Pest Management
conditions: Home vegetable plots across seasonal dry/wet swings
support: Water deeply at the soil base rather than overhead foliage to conserve moisture and curb fungal disease, mulch soil to stabilize temperature and weeds, rotate plant families across seasons, and identify pests before choosing least-toxic controls.
limitations: Untreated rainwater or suspect surface water should not be splashed onto ready-to-eat leafy crops immediately before harvest.
conflicts: None; aligns with FSG-4 clean produce handling.
editorial_note: Grounds resilient low-input gardening and biological pest management.
reviewer: Extension horticulture and integrated pest management

locator: Harvesting Maturity, Curing, and Post-Harvest Handling
conditions: Home garden root crops, winter squash, onions, potatoes, and greens
support: Harvest crops at proper maturity during cool morning hours without bruising, cure storage crops (onions, garlic, winter squash, potatoes) at crop-specific warm/dry conditions before cold storage, and cull any nicked or diseased items for immediate use.
limitations: A single bruised or rotting vegetable spreads decay rapidly across an entire storage bin.
conflicts: None; explains why curing precedes long cold storage.
editorial_note: Anchors harvest-to-storage quality gates in Z14.

locator: Root-Cellar and Cold-Storage Temperature/Humidity Zones
conditions: Basements, root cellars, unheated porches, and insulated cold bins
support: Match stored produce to distinct storage regimes: cold-moist (32–40°F, high humidity for carrots/beets/cabbage), cool-moist (45–50°F for potatoes), cold-dry (32–35°F dry for onions/garlic), and cool-dry (50–55°F dry for winter squash); separate ethylene-producing apples from sensitive vegetables.
limitations: Storing potatoes below 40°F converts starch to sugar; freezing temperatures ruin unhardened stored roots.
conflicts: None; prevents treating one basement temperature as universal for all crops.
editorial_note: Core root-cellar zoning and monitoring evidence in Z14.

locator: Complete Guide to Home Canning > Principle of Tested Protocols
conditions: All residential home canning (boiling-water and pressure canning)
support: Treat every USDA/NCHFP tested canning recipe as a single indivisible system: food pH, piece size, liquid viscosity, jar size, headspace, processing method, pressure/temperature, time, and altitude adjustment must all match the tested protocol.
limitations: Adding extra starch, flour, oil, fats, or altering acid/low-acid ratios slows heat penetration and can cause lethal botulism.
conflicts: Directly prohibits online untested shortcuts and heirloom recipe alterations.
editorial_note: Foundational system-integrity rule across all Z14 canning cards.
reviewer: Food preservation process authority and Extension

locator: Using Pressure Canners; venting; operating at elevation; pressure interruption
conditions: Validated USDA/NCHFP low-acid process, listed equipment, actual elevation
support: Vent continuously for ten minutes before pressurizing. Select the tested product, gauge, altitude, pressure and time combination. If pressure drops below target, restore it and restart the full process time.
limitations: No generic pressure schedule or guarantee. Confirm dial-gauge accuracy according to the reference and obtain Extension guidance on deviations.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Core low-acid botulism-prevention boundary in Z14.
reviewer: Food microbiology and Extension preservation specialist

locator: Using Boiling Water Canners
conditions: Tested high-acid or acidified recipe with a validated water-bath process
support: Use the tested recipe’s equipment and full time including altitude adjustment. Keep required water cover and a continuous boil.
limitations: Atmospheric steam has a separate validated scope; tomato acidification is P22.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Separates high-acid vs low-acid canning gates cleanly.

locator: Headspace, Jar Preparation, Two-Piece Lids, and Cooling Seals
conditions: Mason-type canning jars with two-piece metal lids and screw bands
support: Use true canning jars (never commercial mayonnaise jars), leave exact recipe headspace, remove trapped air bubbles, wipe jar rims clean, tighten bands fingertip-tight only, and let jars cool undisturbed 12–24 hours before checking vacuum seals and removing rings for storage.
limitations: Inverting jars, tightening bands after cooling, or re-using flat sealing lids causes seal failure and silent spoilage.
conflicts: None; directly targets top home-canning mechanical failures.
editorial_note: Grounds jar-seal mechanics and inspection cards in Z14.

locator: Identifying and Handling Spoiled Canned Food
conditions: Suspect home-canned food; identify sealed versus open or leaking without exposure
support: Do not taste. Isolate from people and animals and use current NCHFP or local public-health disposal advice.
limitations: A sealed lid alone cannot establish a safe process. Reprocessing a sound unsealed jar has separate conditions. Suspected exposure is P23.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Anchors spoilage inspection and safe disposal in Z14.

locator: Drying Foods > Pretreatment, Temperature Control, Airflow, and Conditioning
conditions: Electric dehydrators, controlled low ovens, or approved solar dryers for fruits, herbs, vegetables, and jerky
support: Control temperature, low humidity, and continuous airflow simultaneously to remove moisture before spoilage occurs; blanch vegetables where directed, heat meat to safe internal temperatures per NCHFP jerky guidelines, and condition dried fruits to equalize residual moisture before airtight storage.
limitations: Case-hardening (too hot early) traps wet interiors that mold in storage; open-air outdoor drying fails in humid climates like Upper Midwest summers.
conflicts: None; separates safe controlled dehydration from high-risk raw-meat drying.
editorial_note: Grounds dehydration equipment, jerky safety, and moisture-equilibrium checks.
reviewer: Food preservation and food safety specialist

locator: Freezing Foods > Blanching, Packaging, 0°F Storage, and Thawing
conditions: Household freezers maintaining 0°F (-18°C) or lower
support: Blanch most vegetables per tested times to inactivate quality-degrading enzymes, chill promptly, package in moisture-vapor-resistant freezer wrap/containers leaving liquid expansion headspace, freeze at 0°F or below, and thaw safely in the refrigerator (never on the counter).
limitations: Freezing halts microbial growth but does not kill all pathogens; thawed foods require prompt safe cooking/handling.
conflicts: None; connects freezing quality control with Z15 outage loss decisions.
editorial_note: Core freezing and safe thawing evidence in Z14.

locator: Fermenting and Pickling > Salt Ratios, Vinegar Acidity, and Submerged Brine
conditions: Tested lacto-fermented vegetables (sauerkraut/pickles) and vinegar quick-pickles
support: Use standardized 5% acidity vinegar for tested pickle recipes and exact weighed/measured canning-and-pickling salt (not iodized/anti-caking salt) plus clean food-grade crocks and submerged weights for lacto-fermentation at controlled temperatures.
limitations: Altering salt/vinegar ratios or allowing surface mold/scum in warm rooms causes spoilage and unsafe pH drift.
conflicts: None; separates tested fermentation/pickling from improvised brining.
editorial_note: Grounds fermentation, pickling, and acidity verification cards.

locator: Altitude Adjustments, Dial-Gauge Testing, and Extension Verification
conditions: Upper Midwest and elevated U.S. locations (above 1,000 feet elevation)
support: Determine exact local elevation before canning (much of northern and southwestern Minnesota exceeds 1,000 feet), apply USDA altitude increases to boiling-water times or pressure-canner PSI, and use county Extension offices to verify dial gauges and recipes.
limitations: Water boils at lower temperatures as elevation rises, causing under-processing if sea-level times or pressures are used above 1,000 feet.
conflicts: None; highlights Minnesota elevations exceeding 1,000 ft where adjustments apply.
editorial_note: Connects local elevation checks directly to Z14 canning protocols.

locator: Emergency Food Inventory > Non-Perishable Rotation, Dietary Needs, and Tools
conditions: Household multi-day to 30-day emergency pantry planning
support: Build a rotated pantry of familiar shelf-stable foods requiring minimal water and no refrigeration (canned proteins/vegetables, dry grains/legumes, nut butters, infant/medical/pet diets), keep a manual can opener, and mark purchase/rotation dates clearly (FIFO).
limitations: Do not invent unverified multi-decade shelf lives; commercial "Best By" dates reflect quality while damaged, rusted, or dented-seam cans pose safety hazards.
conflicts: None; aligns with FSG-4 and NCHFP storage hygiene.
editorial_note: Grounds household food inventory, FIFO rotation, and can-integrity screening.

locator: Clean, Separate, Cook, Chill > Produce Washing and Cross-Contamination
conditions: Garden-to-kitchen harvesting, food prep, and preservation workspaces
support: Wash hands 20 seconds with soap and safe water, scrub firm produce under running safe water before peeling/cutting, keep raw animal foods strictly separate from ready-to-eat produce, and sanitize prep surfaces and utensils between tasks.
limitations: Washing produce with soap, detergent, or bleach is unsafe and not recommended.
conflicts: None; extends F01–F03 into garden harvest and home preservation.
editorial_note: Anchors kitchen sanitation and cross-contamination barriers in Z14.

locator: Refrigeration Loss, Insulated Coolers, and Discard Boundaries
conditions: Power outages or appliance failures affecting home food stocks
support: Use appliance thermometers in both fridge (≤40°F) and freezer (≤0°F), group frozen foods tightly, avoid opening doors unnecessarily, use block/dry ice with ventilation precautions only when available, and discard perishable items held above 40°F over two hours.
limitations: Dry ice sublimates into carbon dioxide gas and causes severe frostbite on bare skin; handle with gloves and ventilate spaces.
conflicts: None; integrates Z14 cold-chain protection with Z15-R03.
editorial_note: Links food preservation stocks to outage triage and safe discard gates.

locator: Dry Grain, Legume, and Pantry Pest/Moisture Protection
conditions: Cool dry household pantries storing dry beans, grains, flour, and dehydrated produce
support: Store dry staples and dehydrated foods in cool (ideally 50–70°F), dark, dry locations inside airtight food-grade containers to prevent moisture absorption, rancidity, rodents, and pantry insects; inspect periodically for clumping, webbing, or off-odors.
limitations: Heat, humidity, and light degrade nutrients and accelerate fat rancidity in whole grains and nuts far faster than refined staples.
conflicts: None; avoids fabricated 25-year shelf-life promises.
editorial_note: Grounds dry-goods storage, pest exclusion, and spoilage inspection.

locator: Season Extension, Cold Frames, Seed Saving Limits, and Succession Planting
conditions: Northern short-season gardens seeking spring/fall harvest extension
support: Use row covers, low tunnels, or ventilated cold frames to buffer light frosts and stagger fast-maturing crops (succession planting), noting that open-pollinated vs hybrid seeds behave differently if saved and require isolation/dry storage.
limitations: Unvented plastic tunnels overheat rapidly on sunny spring days and cook tender seedlings within an hour.
conflicts: None; grounds realistic northern season extension without overpromising winter yields.
editorial_note: Supports northern resilience and seed-planning cards in Z14.

locator: Unsafe/Unvalidated Canning Methods to Reject
conditions: Home food preservation equipment and method selection
support: Reject oven canning, open-kettle canning, dishwasher canning, microwave canning, and unvalidated electric multicooker pressure canning; dry heat and unpressurized jars fail to destroy C. botulinum spores and risk glass shattering.
limitations: Only independently validated USDA/NCHFP thermal processes establish safe shelf-stable canning.
conflicts: Directly refutes popular social-media and vintage canning shortcuts.
editorial_note: Hard-stop method-rejection card evidence across Z14.

locator: Be Informed > Local Hazard Assessment, Alerts, and Jurisdiction Mapping
conditions: Households preparing for regional multi-hazard emergencies
support: Identify specific local hazards, sign up for county/municipal opt-in alerts alongside WEA/EAS and NOAA Weather Radio, know official evacuation zone labels, and review household plans twice yearly.
limitations: Emergency warning systems, siren policies, and shelter locations vary strictly by county and municipality.
conflicts: None; aligns with T14 and T15.
editorial_note: Establishes jurisdiction-specific alert and planning baseline in Z15.

locator: State overview; temperature and precipitation extremes
conditions: Upper Midwest and Minnesota households across annual hazard seasons
support: Anticipate Minnesota's distinct multi-hazard calendar: spring snowmelt flooding, spring–summer severe thunderstorms, derechos, tornadoes, and extreme heat, wildfire smoke plumes, and autumn–winter blizzards, ice storms, and wind-chill emergencies.
limitations: Weather extremes increasingly occur outside historical peak months; rely on live NWS forecasts over calendar assumptions.
conflicts: None; grounds regional Upper Midwest applicability in Z15.
editorial_note: Connects seasonal hazard preparedness to local agency advisories.

locator: During a Tornado: at home, outside or in a vehicle
conditions: Tornado warning; options depend on location and flood danger
support: Use a sturdy building’s lowest suitable interior area when possible. Mobile homes and overpasses are unsafe. Follow the vehicle or outdoor last-resort branch if sturdy shelter cannot be reached.
limitations: A low outside spot is conditional on safe access and absence of flood danger. Follow local alerts.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Core tornado shelter-selection and post-storm hazard evidence in Z15.

locator: Severe Thunderstorms, Straight-Line Winds, Hail, and Lightning
conditions: Severe Thunderstorm Warnings, derechos, and electrical storms
support: Move indoors to a substantial building immediately when thunder is heard or severe wind warnings issue; stay away from windows, corded appliances, and plumbing during lightning, and avoid downed limbs and energized downed lines after derechos.
limitations: Straight-line derecho winds can rival tornado damage across hundreds of miles and cause multi-day regional power blackouts.
conflicts: None; integrates with E07 and E18.
editorial_note: Grounds severe-storm, hail, and straight-line wind response cards.

locator: Floods: During; Turn Around, Don’t Drown
conditions: Flooded roads or trails, flood alert, or post-flood re-entry
support: Move to safe higher ground when directed, never walk or drive into floodwater, and respect closures and re-entry restrictions.
limitations: Depth examples are warning illustrations, never safe entry thresholds. Trapped or submerged vehicles require emergency help and scene-specific response.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Core flood evacuation, water-avoidance, and safe re-entry evidence.

locator: Wildfires and Air Quality > AQI Categories and Exposure Reduction
conditions: Regional or local wildfire smoke plumes impacting air quality
support: Monitor live official AirNow AQI readings and local health advisories; move indoors with windows/doors closed during Unhealthy AQI levels, limit heavy exertion, and use properly fitted NIOSH-approved N95/P100 particulate respirators if essential outdoor exposure cannot be avoided.
limitations: Surgical masks, bandanas, and dust masks do not seal against fine PM2.5 wildfire smoke particles; N95s do not protect against carbon monoxide or low oxygen.
conflicts: None; complements C19 and READY-WILDFIRE.
editorial_note: Grounds AQI smoke thresholds and respiratory protection limits in Z15.

locator: Create a Clean Room > Indoor Filtration and Recirculation Setup
conditions: Households sheltering indoors during multi-day wildfire smoke events
support: Designate an interior room with few doors/windows, run a properly sized portable HEPA air cleaner (avoiding ozone generators) or set HVAC to recirculate with a MERV-13 filter if system-compatible, and avoid indoor combustion (candles, gas stoves, vacuuming without HEPA) that adds particulates.
limitations: During simultaneous extreme heat and smoke, cooling takes priority if indoor temperatures become dangerous—relocate to a public clean-air cooling center.
conflicts: None; addresses compound smoke-plus-heat emergencies.
editorial_note: Core indoor clean-room assembly and compound-hazard card evidence.
reviewer: Indoor air quality and public health

locator: Stay safe during wildfire; evacuate when directed
conditions: Wildfire threat with local warning and evacuation system
support: Plan to leave early and follow official open routes and local evacuation orders. Return only when allowed.
limitations: Ready–Set–Go is one local vocabulary. Vehicle staging is editorial and does not justify delay after a warning.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Grounds wildfire evacuation readiness and route-abort decisions.
reviewer: Wildland fire management and emergency services

locator: Extreme Heat Waves, Heat Domes, and Power-Outage Cooling Plans
conditions: Prolonged heat advisories, excessive heat warnings, and grid-strain brownouts
support: Identify public cooling centers and air-conditioned backup locations ahead of heat waves, check twice daily on older adults/children/chronically ill neighbors, block solar gain through windows, never leave people or pets in parked vehicles, and activate 911 immediately for heat stroke.
limitations: Electric fans alone do not prevent heat illness when indoor air temperatures climb into extreme heat ranges (above ~95°F) with high humidity.
conflicts: None; aligns with CDC-HEAT, E08, E19, and T09.
editorial_note: Anchors urban/rural heat-wave resilience and vulnerable-neighbor checks.

locator: Blizzards, Ice Storms, and Multi-Day Freezing Blackouts
conditions: Blizzard Warnings, Ice Storm Warnings, and extreme wind-chill emergencies
support: Complete supply, fuel, and medication staging before storm onset, stay off snow/ice-closed roads, prepare safe non-combustion warmth consolidation indoors, keep vents/exits clear of snowdrifts, and evacuate to community warming shelters early if indoor heat fails.
limitations: Ice storms down overhead power lines and trees simultaneously, delaying utility restoration for days across wide areas.
conflicts: None; connects Z15 winter disaster response with Z12/Z13.
editorial_note: Grounds winter-storm travel halts and warming-center transitions.

locator: Preparing for a power outage; during an outage
conditions: Household grid outage; services and backup duration vary
support: Prepare for interruptions to communications, commerce, transport, water and powered medical support.
limitations: Half-tank and cash targets are household planning choices, not predictions of backup limitations.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Drives cascading infrastructure failure and 30-day resilience cards.

locator: Water-System Interruptions and Advisory Compliance
conditions: Municipal main breaks, depressurization, chemical spills, or treatment-plant outages
support: Follow the exact active utility advisory tier (Boil Water, Do Not Drink, or Do Not Use), shut off automatic icemakers/appliances during advisories, flush household pipes strictly per utility clearance instructions after restoration, and rely on stored or agency-distributed potable water during outages.
limitations: Boiling water during a chemical-spill Do Not Drink/Do Not Use notice can volatilize or concentrate contaminants.
conflicts: None; integrates W07 into Z15 infrastructure-disruption scenarios.
editorial_note: Anchors municipal water-outage compliance and safe flushing.

locator: Communications Outages, SMS Priority, and Out-of-Area Rally Contacts
conditions: Regional cellular congestion, tower power loss, or internet blackouts
support: Use short SMS text messages instead of voice calls when cell networks congest, designate an out-of-area contact person to relay family status, establish fixed physical household meeting locations (neighborhood and out-of-town), and monitor battery NOAA/AM-FM radio for official updates.
limitations: Emergency 911 text availability varies by county; confirm local PSAP capability in advance and keep voice dialing primary where reachable.
conflicts: None; builds on T11 and U16.
editorial_note: Grounds communications-failure fallback and group accountability cards.

locator: Before, during and after evacuation
conditions: Official evacuation or a preplanned, safely accessible departure
support: Prepare a go-kit, routes, transport and a contact plan. Follow official routes and use the locally indicated registration or reunification channel.
limitations: Shelter accessibility and animal accommodations require local and ADA guidance; no fixed national website is assumed.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Core evacuation execution and accountability evidence in Z15.

locator: Shelter in place; Stay informed; Next steps
conditions: External airborne chemical release with local shelter-in-place instruction
support: Follow authorities on leaving or sheltering, shutting off outside-air systems, temporary sealing and the all-clear.
limitations: No universal floor, gas behavior, shelter duration or permission to ignore an internal gas leak, CO alarm, fire or evacuation order.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Core hazmat shelter-in-place and ventilation-shutoff boundary.

locator: Vital Documents, Cash Reserves, Insurance, and Post-Disaster Recovery
conditions: 30-day resilience planning and post-disaster household recovery
support: Keep waterproof physical and encrypted offline digital copies of IDs, medical lists, prescriptions, insurance policies, deeds, and emergency contacts alongside small-denomination cash so household transactions and assistance claims survive bank/internet outages.
limitations: Online-only cloud portals are inaccessible during power and telecom outages.
conflicts: None; critical pillar of prolonged 30-day household resilience.
editorial_note: Grounds documentation, cash liquidity, and recovery staging cards.

locator: Pet, Service-Animal, and Vulnerable-Member Accountability
conditions: Households with pets, service animals, children, older adults, or access/functional needs
support: Include leashes, carriers, vaccination records, pet food/water, and pet-friendly shelter lists in household evacuation plans—never leave pets chained or trapped behind; coordinate explicit buddy assignments for children, older adults, and mobility/power-dependent household members.
limitations: General public Red Cross shelters always admit service animals under ADA rules, whereas companion pets often require separate co-located or pet-friendly shelters.
conflicts: None; complements T10 disability planning.
editorial_note: Ensures complete household and vulnerable-group accountability in Z15.
reviewer: Accessible emergency management and animal welfare

locator: Extended 30-Day Resilience, Supply Pacing, and Mutual Aid
conditions: Multi-week regional disruption, supply-chain interruption, or prolonged utility recovery
support: Manage 30-day household resilience through structured inventory tracking, conservative water/fuel/battery rationing, scheduled sanitation and hygiene routines, daily neighborhood wellness checks, and early transition to community distribution hubs before critical reserves run dry.
limitations: Self-reliance plans must remain integrated with municipal/county relief and medical care—isolation without community check-ins increases mortality during prolonged disasters.
conflicts: None; frames 30-day scenarios realistically without doom-isolationism.
editorial_note: Anchors Z15 30-day operations, rationing logs, and community mutual-aid cards.

locator: Recognition of cardiac arrest; Pediatric foreign-body airway obstruction
conditions: Infant or child lay emergency
support: Use pediatric CPR and choking guidance with dispatcher or training. Infant chest thrusts differ from older-child abdominal thrusts; avoid blind sweeps.
limitations: Adult pregnancy and abdominal encirclement exceptions are in M04. Escalate equipment fit and age transitions.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Added in A02 to separate a consequential source boundary.

locator: Recommendations for CPR following drowning
conditions: Adult or child with arrest after removal from water
support: Provide rescue breaths with compressions when able and follow dispatcher; a rescuer unable to give breaths should still start compressions promptly.
limitations: This source addresses resuscitation. Symptomatic submersion requires EMS direction; it does not establish a universal discharge observation time.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Added in A02 to separate a consequential source boundary.

locator: Heat stroke: symptoms and first aid
conditions: Suspected heat stroke; initiate emergency activation and cooling together
support: Call EMS and cool immediately. Select cold-water immersion or cooling with water and airflow based on safe access and airway protection.
limitations: Exertional and classic heat stroke and vulnerable patients warrant specialist cooling protocol review. Avoid oral fluid in impaired alertness.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Added in A02 to separate a consequential source boundary.

locator: First Aid Recommendations; call for help and assess the situation
conditions: Lightning casualty with possible continuing storm exposure
support: Victims retain no charge. Check ongoing danger, report number and status of casualties, call EMS and begin safe dispatcher-guided care.
limitations: No lay permission to enter an active high-risk scene. Multi-casualty triage needs local protocols.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Added in A02 to separate a consequential source boundary.

locator: Precautions; never mix
conditions: Household cleaning and disinfection
support: Never mix bleach with other cleaners or disinfectants. Follow product labeling.
limitations: Protecting and decontaminating exposed people requires Poison Control or emergency guidance.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Added in A02 to separate a consequential source boundary.

locator: If your home flooded; electrical hazards
conditions: Flooded structure or wet electrical equipment
support: Stay away from wet electrical tools or switches and do not operate power while standing in water. Seek qualified clearance before entering or restoring power.
limitations: Qualified structural, gas and sewage cleanup clearance may also be needed.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Added in A02 to separate a consequential source boundary.

locator: Consumer recommendations on storage and preparation
conditions: Potato tubers, including green, bitter or strongly sprouting examples
support: Store potatoes away from light and discard unsuitable green or strongly sprouting tubers and bitter dishes.
limitations: Appearance and greening cannot quantify glycoalkaloids or establish safe intake.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Added in A02 to separate a consequential source boundary.

locator: Quality; Caution; Acidification; pressure alternative
conditions: NCHFP whole, crushed or juiced tomato procedures, recipe and jar size specified
support: Use the complete tested recipe and its acidification choices. Approved pressure alternatives still include acidification. Reject tomatoes from dead or frost-killed vines.
limitations: Does not transfer to salsa, mixed products or untested recipe substitutions.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Added in A02 to separate a consequential source boundary.

locator: Foodborne botulism signs and urgent action
conditions: Possible ingestion of suspect preserved food, particularly with neurologic symptoms
support: Trouble swallowing or breathing, vision changes or weakness can indicate a medical emergency. Seek immediate emergency care for compatible symptoms.
limitations: Symptoms alone cannot establish a diagnosis. Contact local public health or Poison Control for suspected exposures and disposal.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Added in A02 to separate a consequential source boundary.

locator: USDA procedure for meat and poultry jerky
conditions: USDA FSIS home jerky process with wet heat before drying
support: Verify 160°F for meat or 165°F for poultry before dehydration, then use the same procedure’s controlled drying conditions.
limitations: Preheating and drying are linked; texture does not verify pathogen reduction or shelf stability after a deviation.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Added in A02 to separate a consequential source boundary.

locator: If stranded in a vehicle
conditions: Stationary stranded vehicle in an open winter storm, exhaust clear, crew can monitor conditions
support: Stay with the vehicle when safe, alert responders, and follow NWS precautions if running the engine briefly for warmth.
limitations: Do not run with blocked exhaust or suspected CO. Timing does not make idling safe and is no indoor exception.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Added in A02 to separate a consequential source boundary.

locator: Stay indoors and keep cool; seek shelter elsewhere
conditions: Wildfire smoke combined with indoor heat, cooling failure or power outage
support: Use a cooler cleaner-air shelter when the dwelling cannot be kept both cool and adequately protected from smoke.
limitations: No universal ranking of heat and smoke hazards. Follow local evacuation and cooling guidance.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Added in A02 to separate a consequential source boundary.

locator: Stay Cool: indoor fan limits
conditions: Indoor heat protection; general public CDC guidance
support: CDC advises indoor fans only below 90°F; seek cooling and avoid fan-only protection in hotter rooms.
limitations: Humidity, health and local public-health messaging still matter. This is not a safety threshold or active heat-stroke treatment.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Added in A02 to separate a consequential source boundary.

locator: When to call 911; steps to keep the person safe
conditions: Witnessed seizure; community first-aid setting
support: Time the seizure, protect against nearby hazards, avoid restraints and mouth objects and call 911 for listed red flags, including longer than five minutes or breathing or waking difficulty.
limitations: Known personal action plan and dispatcher take precedence. Do not assume that shaking ending means breathing is normal.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Added in A02 to separate a consequential source boundary.

locator: Treating low blood sugar; treating severely low blood sugar
conditions: Suspected hypoglycemia with known diabetes
support: Follow the person’s plan. Give fast-acting sugar only if awake and able to swallow. Severe symptoms, inability to swallow or unconsciousness warrant prompt emergency help.
limitations: No dose or schedule is implied for every patient. Rescue glucagon use depends on patient-specific prescription, training and emergency instructions.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Added in A02 to separate a consequential source boundary.

locator: Conditions for safe atmospheric steam canning
conditions: Approved high-acid or acidified food and tested adapted boiling-water recipe
support: Use the research-tested temperature, steam and equipment conditions and limit total processing to 45 minutes or less including elevation.
limitations: No substitution for a pressure canner or allowance for uncertain temperature or running dry.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Added in A02 to separate a consequential source boundary.

locator: Ready-to-feed preference and special considerations
conditions: Formula-fed infant in an emergency with uncertain water or sanitation
support: Use ready-to-feed if available, especially for infants under two months, premature infants and those with weakened immune systems. If powder is necessary, follow the CDC and local instructions for safe water, preparation, hygiene and storage.
limitations: Powder is not sterile. Boiling the water does not by itself address the powder, special population or chemical-water issues.
conflicts: See A02 claim audit for boundaries.
editorial_note: Added in A02 to separate a consequential source boundary.

locator: Geologic provinces and bedrock mapping
conditions: Minnesota and Upper Midwest regional bedrock/glacial terrain
support: Minnesota spans Precambrian Canadian Shield igneous/metamorphic rock, Midcontinent Rift volcanics, Paleozoic sedimentary strata, and Pleistocene glacial drift.
limitations: Surficial glacial till frequently conceals underlying bedrock; local geologic maps and field verification remain necessary.
conflicts: Generalized state maps do not confirm outcrop-scale rock composition.
editorial_note: Bounds Z08 regional geology framing.

locator: Glacial drift and landscape materials
conditions: Glacial till, moraines, outwash, and lake-plain deposits
support: Glacial transport mixes erratics and cobbles from distant source formations across Minnesota soils and stream beds.
limitations: Cobble location does not prove local bedrock origin or uniform internal stone integrity.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Separates erratic cobbles from bedrock strata.

locator: Igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rock classes
conditions: Field rock class screening without laboratory petrography
support: Observable grain interlocking, layering, bedding, or foliation helps separate broad rock classes.
limitations: Weathered rinds and fine-grained dark rocks frequently mimic other classes visually; hand-lens inspection is preliminary only.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Establishes non-destructive classification limits.

locator: Hardness, luster, streak, and fracture vs cleavage
conditions: Non-destructive mineral observation with simple field cues
support: Scratch hardness, unglazed streak, luster, and fracture-versus-cleavage patterns narrow candidate mineral groups.
limitations: Field scratch checks cannot establish chemical purity, trace heavy metals, or absence of hazardous fibers.
conflicts: Color alone is unreliable across quartz, calcite, and feldspar varieties.
editorial_note: Core Z08 mineral screening basis.

locator: Chert, jasper, agate, and quartz occurrences
conditions: Upper Midwest siliceous cobbles and sedimentary nodules
support: Cryptocrystalline quartz varieties (chert, flint, jasper, agate) are hard silica rocks showing conchoidal fracture rather than planar cleavage.
limitations: Visual similarity to fine-grained quartzite, basalt, or glass does not confirm thermal stability or structural suitability.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Anchors Z08 siliceous stone identification.

locator: Overview; Exposure
conditions: Silica-bearing material disturbed by cutting, grinding, or similar dust-producing work
support: Respirable crystalline silica exposure can cause silicosis and other disease. Avoid creating dust during field recognition.
limitations: Hazardous particles may be invisible. Wind, casual wetting and a mask alone do not establish exposure control.
conflicts: Conditions are recorded in the A03 audit.
editorial_note: Mandatory Z08 silica/eye safety gate.

locator: Naturally occurring asbestos and fibrous minerals
conditions: Outcrops, fibrous veins, serpentinite, and iron-formation rock
support: Naturally occurring asbestiform mineral fibers pose severe inhalation risks if disturbed, broken, or abraded.
limitations: Field sight alone cannot distinguish benign fibrous minerals from regulated asbestos; leave fibrous mineral veins undisturbed.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Mandatory Z08 mineral-fiber stop rule.

locator: 36 CFR 2.1 natural resource collecting prohibitions
conditions: National Parks, Monuments, and federal recreation areas
support: Collecting rocks, minerals, fossils, wood, or natural specimens is prohibited on National Park System lands unless specifically authorized.
limitations: Rules vary across USFS, BLM, state, tribal, county, and private lands; check the governing land manager before taking any sample.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Prevents unlawful federal resource extraction.

locator: State park natural-feature protection
conditions: Minnesota State Parks and Recreation Areas
support: Removing rocks, minerals, soil, or live vegetation from Minnesota State Parks is prohibited to protect natural resources.
limitations: Verify jurisdiction boundaries before picking up specimens even along shorelines or trails.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Bounds state-park material collection.

locator: No collecting plants, animals, rocks or fossils; Foraging
conditions: Minnesota Scientific and Natural Areas, subject to the actual site rules
support: Leave natural features in place unless the site lists an applicable exception or there is a valid authorization.
limitations: Certain named sites have limited berry or mushroom exceptions. They do not extend to rocks or general digging.
conflicts: Conditions are recorded in the A03 audit.
editorial_note: Enforces SNA zero-collection boundaries.

locator: Lawful public-land gravel-pit and road-cut rock collecting limits
conditions: Unrestricted public gravel areas and authorized private land
support: Where lawful, rock hounding requires landowner permission on private land and compliance with local safety and collecting limits.
limitations: Private property, active quarries, road right-of-way hazards, and tribal lands carry separate prohibitions and trespass penalties.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Clarifies lawful vs prohibited rock collection.

locator: Soil contamination and urban/industrial lead hazards
conditions: Soils near historic structures, roadways, mines, or industrial sites
support: Soils and clays near older painted structures, smelters, tailings, or roadways may harbor lead or industrial contaminants.
limitations: Visual texture or color cannot detect lead, arsenic, or chemical contaminants; do not use unverified soil/clay for cookware or food contact.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Separates clay plasticity checks from chemical safety.

locator: Rocks and Minerals overview
conditions: Unrated stones near a fire or during thermal cycling
support: Use agency-approved fire facilities and keep people away from cracking or shifting material.
limitations: Editorial avoidance. The cited geology overview does not establish a safe rock type, moisture test or heating threshold.
conflicts: Conditions are recorded in the A03 audit.
editorial_note: Reinforces Z03/Z08 wet-rock spalling stop.

locator: Metallic ores, sulfides, and heavy-metal mineral toxicity
conditions: Unidentified metallic-luster minerals, tailings, or bright oxidized crusts
support: Sulfide ores and metallic minerals can contain lead, arsenic, mercury, or copper compounds hazardous via dust or hand-to-mouth transfer.
limitations: Do not taste, lick, burn, or process unidentified metallic or brightly crusted minerals; wash hands after handling.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Blocks hazardous mineral extraction/handling.

locator: Regional wood species, grain, bark, and moisture variability
conditions: Dead downed wood and natural bast fibers in Upper Midwest forests
support: Wood density, grain straightness, resin content, and decay state vary widely by species, tree part, and moisture history.
limitations: Visual grain inspection cannot certify structural load capacity; avoid cutting live trees where prohibited and reject punky or cracked wood.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Reconciles B007 wood notes with material limits.

locator: Sedimentary limestone, sandstone, and shale permeability
conditions: Southeastern Minnesota karst, bluff, and river-valley sedimentary strata
support: Sandstone, limestone, and shale differ sharply in cementation, porosity, and fissility, governing weathering and cliff instability.
limitations: Karst bluffs and fractured shales shed rockfall unpredictably; visual inspection cannot certify slope or load stability.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Covers Upper Midwest sedimentary rock hazards.

locator: Minnesota geological mapping and educational materials
conditions: Unverified clay or soil
support: Texture and workability observations are screening cues. Unknown material does not qualify for food contact or heated service.
limitations: A soil map or field texture cannot verify lead leaching, firing behavior or sanitation.
conflicts: Conditions are recorded in the A03 audit.
editorial_note: Bounds Z08 clay identification vs cookware claims.

locator: Natural plant fiber harvest limits and conservation ethics
conditions: Bast fibers, rushes, sedges, and woody stems in regional biomes
support: Harvesting fibrous plants without landowner permission or in protected native plant communities damages ecosystems and may violate law.
limitations: Strength of hand-twisted plant cordage varies sharply with retting, moisture, and knots; never assign life-safety loads.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Connects Z08 fibers to Z09 load limits and law.

locator: Specimen documentation, scale, and locality recording
conditions: Documenting geological specimens for reference or museum review
support: Recording locality, host formation, metric scale, fresh vs weathered surface, and non-destructive traits preserves scientific value.
limitations: A photograph or hand sample without locality and scale rarely permits definitive identification of fine-grained rocks.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Defines Z08 specimen voucher protocol.

locator: Iron-formation magnetism and compass deflection awareness
conditions: Northern Minnesota iron ranges and mafic volcanic rock
support: Magnetite-bearing iron formations and gabbro outcrops can visibly deflect magnetic compass needles locally.
limitations: Deflection varies over short distances; cross-check bearings against terrain and non-magnetic cues rather than assuming uniform declination.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Cross-links Z08 geology with Z11 compass limits.

locator: Licensing, seasons, limits, and waterbody-specific rules
conditions: Minnesota angling across inland, border, and designated waters
support: Anglers must hold a valid license unless explicitly exempt and verify current season dates, possession limits, size slots, and special waterbody rules before fishing.
limitations: Regulations change annually and differ on border waters, trout streams, and tribal/ceded territories; no emergency creates an automatic legal exemption.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Establishes Z06 fishing authority gate.
reviewer: Minnesota DNR fisheries and legal reviewer

locator: Hunting licenses, zones, seasons, and legal methods
conditions: Minnesota big game, small game, and bird hunting
support: Hunters must verify current license, permit-area, season, legal-hours, blaze-clothing, and method rules with the governing authority prior to afield activity.
limitations: Private-land trespass law, municipal ordinances, and tribal jurisdiction apply separately; emergencies do not suspend wildlife law.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Establishes Z06 hunting authority gate.

locator: Four fundamental firearm safety rules and certification
conditions: Any firearm handling, transport, or field carry
support: Treat every firearm as loaded, keep the muzzle in a safe direction, keep finger off the trigger until ready to shoot, and verify target and what is beyond it.
limitations: Certification is required by age/statute in Minnesota; written summaries never substitute for formal certified safety instruction.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Mandatory Z06 bounded weapon-safety gate.
reviewer: Certified hunter-education and firearm safety instructor

locator: Waterbody-specific fish consumption advisories (mercury, PFAS, PCBs)
conditions: Consuming Minnesota caught freshwater fish
support: MDH issues species-, size-, and waterbody-specific meal-frequency limits for mercury, PCBs, and PFAS, with stricter limits for pregnant/nursing people and children under 15.
limitations: Visual fish health and water clarity cannot detect mercury, PFAS, or PCBs; check current MDH waterbody lookup before eating caught fish.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Mandatory Z06 public-health fish advisory gate.

locator: Trimming fat and skin limits for organic contaminants vs mercury
conditions: Cleaning and preparing advisory-screened freshwater fish
support: Trimming belly/dorsal fat and removing skin can reduce fat-soluble PCBs, but mercury binds in muscle tissue and cannot be trimmed or cooked out.
limitations: Cleaning methods never replace checking waterbody-specific advisories or respecting do-not-eat notices.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Distinguishes PCB trimming from mercury persistence.

locator: Positive fish species identification before keeping catch
conditions: Identifying regional game, rough, and protected fish species
support: Accurate species identification using fin counts, mouth structure, markings, and body profile is mandatory to comply with limits and protected-species rules.
limitations: Juveniles and hybrids can resemble restricted species; release immediately when positive identification is uncertain.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Connects Z06 identification to lawful harvest.

locator: Clean, Drain, Dry aquatic invasive species law
conditions: Moving watercraft, angling gear, waders, or bait between waterbodies
support: Minnesota law requires cleaning aquatic plants/zebra mussels from gear, draining all water with plugs removed, and disposing of unwanted bait in trash.
limitations: Never transport live fish or lake water away from infested waters except under explicit statutory permit.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Mandatory Z06 conservation/AIS compliance.

locator: Chronic Wasting Disease surveillance zones and carcass rules
conditions: Harvesting cervids in Minnesota CWD management/control zones
support: DNR designates CWD zones with mandatory sampling, carcass movement restrictions, and proper disposal rules.
limitations: Infected deer can appear completely healthy; check current zone maps and test before consuming venison from affected areas.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Core Z06 CWD regulation and safety rule.

locator: Reducing risk in places with CWD activity; testing
conditions: Deer or elk taken in a CWD area, plus regional rules
support: Avoid sick and found-dead animals, minimize nervous tissue contact, use suitable gloves, and follow testing guidance. Do not eat positive animals.
limitations: A negative test does not establish safety against all hazards. Do not use cooking as a substitute for CWD guidance.
conflicts: Conditions are recorded in the A03 audit.
editorial_note: Reinforces Z06 prion hygiene boundary.

locator: Implications for Public Health Practice
conditions: Wild game in the context of Trichinella prevention, especially bear and similar high-risk game
support: CDC reports the public-health recommendation of at least 165°F (74°C), verified by a food thermometer. Freezing wild game is unreliable.
limitations: No guarantee against pathogens or cross-contamination. Keep raw meat and juices separate from other foods.
conflicts: Conditions are recorded in the A03 audit.
editorial_note: Critical Z06 wild-game parasite safety rule.

locator: Tularemia precautions with wild rabbits, hares, and rodents
conditions: Field handling of small game and carcasses
support: Wear impervious gloves when handling wild rabbits/rodents, avoid sick or sluggish animals, and cook meat thoroughly; bacteria can enter through skin breaks or aerosols.
limitations: Do not handle found-dead wildlife; seek medical evaluation promptly for fever or skin ulcers after exposure.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Critical Z06 small-game zoonosis safety gate.

locator: Black bear encounter avoidance and attractant control
conditions: Campsites, fishing shores, and trails in bear range
support: Store food, fish waste, and scented items securely; make calm noise in thick cover, back away slowly without running, and never approach cubs.
limitations: Bear behavior varies with habituation and food stress; carry and know local bear-deterrent rules where appropriate.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Core Z06 wildlife encounter avoidance.

locator: Gray wolf legal status and encounter guidance
conditions: Northern Minnesota wolf range
support: Gray wolves are legally protected in Minnesota under federal/state status; maintain distance, keep pets leashed, secure attractants, and report bold behavior to DNR.
limitations: Never feed, approach, or attempt to harass protected predators; verify current legal status before any assumption.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Protects endangered/managed carnivores and bystanders.

locator: Migratory Bird Treaty Act federal protections
conditions: All native migratory birds, nests, feathers, and eggs
support: Federal law prohibits taking, possessing, or disturbing protected migratory birds, nests, or eggs outside regulated hunting seasons and federal permits.
limitations: Waterfowl hunting requires both state licenses and a federal Duck Stamp plus non-toxic shot rules.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Enforces federal migratory bird law.

locator: Turn In Poachers (TIP) and wildlife incident reporting
conditions: Suspected wildlife violations, injured game, or unsafe incidents
support: Observe from a safe distance, record location, time, descriptions, and license plates without confronting suspects, and report to MN DNR TIP or Conservation Officers.
limitations: Do not pursue armed or hostile individuals or disturb physical evidence.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Defines Z06/Z07 non-confrontational incident reporting.

locator: Mammal ecology, seasonal movement, and sign interpretation
conditions: Reading wildlife tracks, scat, browse, and trail patterns
support: Substrate moisture, snow crust, and animal gait distort track dimensions; combine multiple signs and habitat context rather than single prints.
limitations: Never handle unknown scat barehanded due to parasite eggs (e.g., Baylisascaris); sign interpretation is ecological observation, not harvest authorization.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Grounds Z06 tracking in ecology and hygiene.

locator: Big-game seasonal ecology and field-hygiene cooling
conditions: White-tailed deer habitat, rut/winter yarding, and meat spoilage limits
support: Rapid cooling below 40 F, keeping carcasses clean of gut contents and dirt, and protecting meat from insects prevent bacterial spoilage.
limitations: Warm autumn weather accelerates spoilage within hours; abandon harvest if safe transport and cooling cannot be achieved.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Connects Z06 harvest to cold-chain food safety.
