locator: Waterfowl cold-water capsizing and non-toxic shot compliance
conditions: Wetland and open-water fall waterfowl environments
support: Cold-water immersion, overloaded boats, and wading drop-offs cause severe fatalities; wear flotation, check forecasts, and verify federal non-toxic shot and species limits.
limitations: Emergencies and weather shifts override harvest goals; stay ashore in high wind or unverified ice.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Reconciles B013 P15-P16 with Z06 water/ice limits.

locator: Minnesota trapping licensing, seasons, and statutory limits
conditions: Any regulated trapping activity or legal reference in Minnesota
support: Trapping is strictly regulated by license, season, species, trap type, set location, check intervals, and landowner permission; unauthorized trapping is illegal.
limitations: Emergency narratives never create an exemption to set traps or snares; verify current statute and DNR handbook every season.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Primary Z07 legal boundary.
reviewer: Wildlife law and DNR enforcement reviewer

locator: AFWA Best Management Practices for animal welfare and selectivity
conditions: Evaluating trapping principles, welfare, and non-target risk
support: AFWA BMPs evaluate regulated devices on animal welfare, efficiency, selectivity, user safety, and practicality through scientific testing.
limitations: Improvised traps and snares lack scientific welfare testing and selectivity controls, causing severe injury and non-target capture.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Anchors Z07 welfare & conceptual classification without building instructions.

locator: Endangered Species Act strict take prohibitions
conditions: Federal threatened and endangered species habitats (e.g., Canada lynx)
support: Incidental or intentional capture, injury, or harassment of federally listed species violates the Endangered Species Act and triggers strict reporting and gear restrictions.
limitations: Trapping zones near lynx or listed-species ranges carry additional federal/state exclusion rules.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Enforces ESA species protection in Z07.

locator: State endangered, threatened, and special-concern species
conditions: Habitats supporting state-listed mammals, birds, reptiles, and amphibians
support: Unselective devices endanger state-listed species including raptors, mustelids, and turtles.
limitations: Verify protected-species distribution and never disturb protected habitats or dens.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Protects state-listed nongame species.

locator: Nongame wildlife protection and ecological role
conditions: Non-harvested wildlife across forests, wetlands, and prairies
support: Most wild mammals, songbirds, raptors, and reptiles are legally protected nongame species that may not be captured or killed.
limitations: Ecological stewardship prioritizes observation and avoidance over capture.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Frames Z07 ecological ethics.

locator: Reporting injured, orphaned, or accidentally trapped wildlife
conditions: Discovering a trapped or injured wild animal in the field
support: Maintain safe distance to avoid bites, rabies, and stress to the animal; note GPS/location and contact a Conservation Officer or licensed wildlife rehabilitator.
limitations: Never attempt barehanded release of distressed carnivores, raptors, or large mammals.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Establishes Z07 incidental-capture reporting protocol.

locator: Hunting and trapping
conditions: Minnesota SNA and adjacent state land
support: Verify the current rules for the precise site. Minnesota DNR lists trapping rules by SNA.
limitations: Use separate state-park, recreation-area, and other land rules. Private permission does not supersede law.
conflicts: Conditions are recorded in the A03 audit.
editorial_note: Clarifies where bystanders/pets may encounter lawful sets.

conditions: National Park System unit and its current authorizations
support: Taking wildlife is generally prohibited except when authorized under the governing framework. Verify any unit-specific hunting or trapping authorization.
limitations: Section 2.1 addresses natural resources and section 2.2 addresses wildlife. The rule is not permission outside the unit.
conflicts: Conditions are recorded in the A03 audit.
editorial_note: Federal land-boundary clarity.

locator: Reporting illegal, unmarked, or abandoned traps and snares
conditions: Encountering suspected unlawful, out-of-season, or unsafe sets
support: Do not touch, spring, or steal equipment; photograph from a safe distance with location coordinates and report to MN DNR TIP or local law enforcement.
limitations: Tampering with lawful traps can be illegal and risks severe hand injury from stored spring energy.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Protects bystanders from injury and legal liability.

locator: Human and pet hazard recognition around lawful trapping areas
conditions: Walking dogs or hiking in open public-use lands during furbearer seasons
support: Keep dogs on short leashes on open multi-use lands during autumn/winter trapping seasons, avoid bait piles and shoreline culverts, and carry vet contact info.
limitations: Body-gripping and cable devices present rapid fatal risk to unleashed pets; prevention via leashing is far safer than emergency release.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Core Z07 bystander & pet hazard prevention.

locator: Conceptual classification of historic vs regulated capture categories
conditions: Educational overview of mechanical hazard types without construction specs
support: Historical and regulated devices fall into restraining (foothold, cage, cable restraint) and killing (body-grip) hazard classes with distinct spring-energy risks.
limitations: Conceptual awareness supports hazard recognition only and must never include trigger dimensions, wire specs, or placement instructions.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Enforces Z07 no-actionable-construction editorial boundary.

locator: Attractant, bait-site, and carrion encounter avoidance
conditions: Field travel near carrion, bait stations, or water-edge cubbies
support: Strong odors, feathers, flagged stakes, or disturbed shoreline funnels can indicate carrion, bear feeding sites, or active regulated sets.
limitations: Route wide around suspect attractants and keep companions and pets close.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Hazard-recognition field cue for Z07.

locator: Zero-disturbance scientific preserve ethics
conditions: Sensitive habitats, wetlands, and rare-species corridors
support: Natural-area conservation prohibits altering vegetation, digging pits, or leaving wire/cordage debris that entangles wildlife indefinitely.
limitations: Abandoned wire or monofilament creates persistent ghost-entanglement hazards.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Addresses ghost-gear and environmental restriction.

locator: Raptor and migratory bird vulnerability to exposed bait sets
conditions: Woodlands, wetlands, and prairie edges with raptors and scavengers
support: Exposed meat baits attract protected hawks, owls, eagles, and scavengers, creating severe federal and state non-target capture hazards.
limitations: Federal MBTA and Bald and Golden Eagle Protection Act impose strict penalties for protected bird injury.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Highlights avian non-target vulnerability.

locator: Minnesota Biodiversity Atlas regional occurrence and specimen data
conditions: Documenting regional plant and fungal distribution in Minnesota
support: Regional atlas records establish verified county-level occurrences and phenology windows for Minnesota plants and fungi.
limitations: Occurrence maps confirm regional presence only; they never confirm a field specimen identity or consumption suitability.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Anchors Z05 Minnesota regional taxonomy.

locator: Curated herbarium and fungarium voucher specimen standards
conditions: Corroborating species traits against documented physical vouchers
support: Curated herbarium and fungarium vouchers link accepted scientific names, collection locality, habitat, and morphology to verifiable specimens.
limitations: Image-search labels and crowd-sourced guesses cannot substitute for vouchered keys and qualified taxonomic review.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Core P19-A voucher discipline.

locator: Accepted botanical nomenclature, authorities, and synonyms
conditions: Standardizing plant scientific names across regional floras
support: Tracking accepted Latin binomials, taxonomic authorities, and legacy synonyms prevents dangerous common-name confusion.
limitations: Common names like hemlock, nightshade, elder, or wild carrot refer to unrelated toxic and non-toxic taxa across regions.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Prevents common-name misidentification.

locator: Integrated Taxonomic Information System verification
conditions: Cross-checking scientific binomials and taxonomic hierarchy
support: Standardized taxonomic identifiers keep plant and fungal hierarchies auditable across updates.
limitations: Taxonomic revisions split or reassign species; record check date and authority on every profile.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Maintains taxonomic schema rigor.

locator: Separate fungal voucher collections and microscopic/macro traits
conditions: Documenting macrofungi across North American collections
support: Fungal taxonomy requires distinct anatomical schemas (cap, gills/pores/teeth, attachment, ring, volva, spore print, substrate, and often microscopy).
limitations: Fungal species complexes frequently overlap macroscopically; photos alone cannot confirm edibility.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Keeps botanical and fungal schemas separate.

locator: 2018 incident and cited 2006 Minnesota outbreak
conditions: Minnesota case evidence from distinct incidents
support: The 2018 report describes A. muscaria intoxication. It separately cites a 2006 Minnesota outbreak involving A. bisporigera and amatoxin.
limitations: Do not conflate the clinical syndromes, use the reports to identify a specimen, or infer a reliable symptom clock.
conflicts: Conditions are recorded in the A03 audit.
editorial_note: Critical Minnesota fungal hazard evidence.

locator: Amanita phalloides outbreak and amatoxin lethality (MMWR 75:20)
conditions: Recognizing lethal Amanita lookalike risk and cooking myths
support: Amatoxins in death cap and destroying angel species survive boiling, freezing, and drying; misidentification causes acute liver failure and death.
limitations: Never rely on folklore tests, boiling, peeling, or visual similarity to safe regional species.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Prohibits boiling/peeling mushroom myths.

locator: Mushroom poisoning syndrome classes and specimen retention
conditions: Evaluating suspected wild fungal exposure
support: Mushroom toxins span distinct syndromes (amatoxins, gyromitrin, orellanine, muscarine, ibotenic acid, GI irritants) with onset from minutes to days.
limitations: Save remaining uneaten mushroom pieces in a paper bag (not sealed plastic) for mycologist identification if exposure occurs, and call Poison Control immediately.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Grounds Z05 fungal toxicology & emergency referral.

locator: When to call 911; get help from poison experts
conditions: Suspected poisoning in the United States
support: Call 911 for collapse, seizure, trouble breathing or inability to wake. Otherwise promptly call Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222.
limitations: Use route- and substance-specific advice. Do not wait for symptoms or collect unknown material if doing so risks exposure or delays care.
conflicts: Conditions are recorded in the A03 audit.
editorial_note: Mandatory Z05 poison-response escalation.

locator: Poisonous plants, berries, and dose-dependent pediatric risk
conditions: Household, trailside, and wild berries, seeds, and foliage
support: Many attractive wild berries, seeds, and roots contain cardiac glycosides, alkaloids, or oxalates that cause rapid toxicity, especially in children.
limitations: Never sample unknown plants; recognition and consumption suitability remain separate decisions.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Separates recognition from consumption.

locator: Maine case description and editorial note
conditions: Suspected water-hemlock ingestion
support: Water hemlock ingestion can cause severe poisoning including seizures. Suspected poisoning needs prompt emergency or poison-centre advice.
limitations: The case concerns Cicuta maculata. It cannot identify a plant outdoors or establish Conium toxin mechanism, dose, or onset.
conflicts: Conditions are recorded in the A03 audit.
editorial_note: Mandatory Z05 lethal Apiaceae stop rule.

locator: Toxic plant dermatitis and hemlock contact/ingestion hazards
conditions: Field work around poison ivy, poison sumac, wild parsnip, and hemlocks
support: Urushiol oils in Toxicodendron species cause severe allergic contact dermatitis; burning vines aerosolizes toxic smoke that damages lungs.
limitations: Never burn unknown vines or brush piles; wash exposed skin promptly with cool water and soap.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Covers Z05 contact/inhalation plant hazards.

locator: Poisonous plant recognition and avoidance for outdoor workers
conditions: Woodland, edge, and wetland fieldwork
support: Learn local poisonous plants by leaf arrangement, stem traits, and habitat before field work, wear protective layers, and wash contaminated tools and clothing separately.
limitations: Single-season familiarity fails in winter when woody vines and dormant stems retain active urushiol.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Supports multi-season toxic plant awareness.

locator: Wild parsnip (Pastinaca sativa) phytophotodermatitis
conditions: Sunny roadsides, prairies, and disturbed meadows in Minnesota
support: Sap from wild parsnip contains furocoumarins that react with sunlight to cause painful chemical burns and blistering.
limitations: Avoid bare-skin contact with yellow-umbel roadside stems; wash sap immediately and shield exposed skin from sunlight.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Specific Minnesota photodermatitis lookalike warning.

locator: Common buckthorn (Rhamnus cathartica) dark berry lookalike
conditions: Minnesota woodlands, edges, and thickets
support: Common buckthorn bears clusters of dark purplish-black berries with sub-opposite leaves and terminal twig spines; fruit causes severe gastrointestinal purging.
limitations: Frequently confused with chokecherry, serviceberry, or elderberry by casual observers; verify leaf arrangement, thorns, and seed count.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Key Minnesota dark-berry toxic lookalike.

locator: Native Minnesota trees: bark, buds, leaves, cones, and nuts
conditions: Identifying oaks, pines, birches, maples, basswood, walnut, and spruce across seasons
support: Reliable tree identification integrates leaf/needle arrangement, bud scales, bark pattern, fruit/cone structure, and habitat across seasons.
limitations: Tree nuts and bark materials can require specific processing (e.g., tannin leaching) and remain on consumption HOLD until reviewed.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Anchors Z05 regional tree-food & bark profiles.

locator: Protected rare plants and harvest conservation boundaries
conditions: Minnesota endangered, threatened, and special-concern flora
support: Rare native plants (e.g., wild ginseng, orchids, prairie perennials) carry strict legal protections against digging or harvest.
limitations: Never dig unknown roots or bulbs on public land; verify legal collecting status before touching any specimen.
conflicts: None noted.
editorial_note: Prevents illegal digging of protected flora.

locator: Native plant communities and habitat-context screening

locator: Overview; how can I find out if my ceramicware are safe?
conditions: Unknown or decorative ceramicware and food or beverage contact
support: Lead can leach from some ceramicware into food or drink. Decorative or unverified ceramicware is unsuitable for food-contact permission based on appearance.
limitations: This FDA guidance addresses lead and ceramicware. It does not prove that specific wild clay contains lead or qualify firing or thermal strength.

locator: Preparing Your Garden and Recommendations Based on the Amount of Lead in Your Soil
conditions: Garden lead-exposure guidance after soil testing
support: EPA recommends clean soil above visible fabric, limiting dust and following test-based restrictions. Above 400 ppm, EPA advises shallow roots only with 16 inches of clean soil above fabric, or containers.
limitations: Garden exposure advice, not a land remediation standard or guarantee. Follow the local authority for site-specific guidance.
conflicts: Some site thresholds differ by jurisdiction.
editorial_note: A04 raised-bed correction.

locator: Chapter 4 Section III, 4-12 Bowline: tying steps and checkpoints (pages 4-13 to 4-14)
conditions: Tying a single fixed loop in the end of a rope
support: The bowline ties a single fixed loop in the end of a rope. Checkpoints: the bight is locked into place by a loop; the short portion of the bight is inside the fixed loop; a minimum 4-inch pigtail remains after the overhand safety is tied.
limitations: Written for trained users of mountaineering rope. Gives no rating for utility cord and does not make an improvised loop suitable for life support. Superseded 2002 edition; the 2012 TC 3-97.61 wording was not checked.
conflicts: None; the card sequence and inside-tail finish match these checkpoints.
editorial_note: Grounds the Z09-P14 structure, tail position and stopper backup. The W2C plate crossing order is checked against this structure.

locator: Chapter 4 Section III, 4-14 Figure-eight retrace (figure-eight knot description) and 4-20 Figure-eight loop checkpoints (pages 4-15, 4-21 to 4-22)
conditions: Tying a figure-eight knot in a line end or a figure-eight loop in a doubled line
support: A figure-eight knot is formed by making a loop, wrapping the working end around the standing part and routing it through the loop. The figure-eight loop forms a fixed loop; the ropes in the loop are parallel and do not cross over each other, and the knot is tightly dressed.
limitations: Written for mountaineering rope. No rating for utility cord, grommet size or pull-through resistance. Superseded 2002 edition.
conflicts: None.
editorial_note: Grounds the Z09-P15 stopper and loop structures. The grommet-blocking use of the stopper remains an editorial adaptation.

locator: How To Get Your Map and Compass To Face the Same Direction (orientation steps)
conditions: Orienting a paper map with a baseplate compass
support: Place the baseplate parallel to the map north-south neat line; turn the dial until ring north agrees with map north and correct for declination (subtract if positive, add if negative; an adjustable compass already calibrated needs no correction); turn map and compass together until the red needle overlays the orienting arrow, avoiding metal. The map is then oriented to true north; compare surrounding features with the map.
limitations: Undated web page. The declination value must come from a current model or map margin. Does not address grid north.
conflicts: None; consistent with the N08 and T08 declination convention.
editorial_note: Grounds the Z11-R05 orientation steps and the W2C plate dial, needle and neat-line relationships.

locator: Chapter 3 Theory of Backflow and Backsiphonage (page 12, Figure 7); Chapter 4 Air Gap and Hose Bibb Vacuum Breakers (pages 16 and 18)
conditions: Household hoses, buckets and auxiliary water near potable plumbing
support: Backsiphonage is reverse flow caused by atmospheric pressure forcing a pollutant liquid toward a potable supply under vacuum, for example through a submerged hose end when supply pressure drops. Air gaps are non-mechanical backflow preventers effective against backsiphonage and backpressure. Hose bibb vacuum breakers attach to hose faucets and vent to atmosphere when supply pressure is off; they are not backpressure devices.
limitations: Guidance manual for programs and plumbers. Device choice and installation follow local plumbing code and licensed plumbers; fixed air-gap dimensions apply to fixtures, not hand-held hoses.
conflicts: None.
editorial_note: Grounds the Z13-P44 backsiphonage path, vacuum breaker and air gap.

locator: Pressure Tanks (page 16)
conditions: Private well systems with a pressure tank and pressure switch
support: A pressure tank stores water under pressure and supplies it when the pump is not running; a pressure switch starts and stops the pump at preset pressures. The drawdown delivered between pump shutoff and restart is much smaller than the tank; common 20- to 44-gallon tanks have a drawdown of 5 to 16 gallons.
limitations: Settings and tank sizes vary by system. The handbook does not address power outages directly; electrical and well work requires licensed contractors.
conflicts: None.
editorial_note: Grounds the Z13-P41 outage relationship and the typical drawdown range.
reviewer: Licensed well contractor and master electrician

locator: Choosing and Using Fire Extinguishers: when to use (checklist), PASS steps, extinguisher classes
conditions: Deciding whether to use a portable extinguisher on a home fire
support: Use an extinguisher only when others are alerted, the fire department has been called, the user is physically able, the fire is small and contained to one object or surface such as a pan or wastebasket, the user is safe from smoke and has a clear escape route; otherwise alert others, leave and call 911. PASS: pull the pin, aim low at the base, squeeze slowly and evenly, sweep side to side. Multipurpose A-B-C units cover most home fires.
limitations: Young children and older adults should not use extinguishers. The page does not address water on grease fires.
conflicts: None.
editorial_note: Grounds the Z13-P57 decision checklist and PASS steps.
reviewer: Fire service and residential fire safety

locator: Consumers Warned Against Storing Gasoline (news release, July 30, 1979)
conditions: Household gasoline storage
support: Gasoline vapors are heavier than air and can travel to ignition sources such as pilot lights in stoves and furnaces. Keep storage cans outdoors, far from living quarters and ignition sources, such as in a well-ventilated shed; never store gasoline in the house or a vehicle; keep sturdy, tightly sealed containers.
limitations: 1979 release; its container-material advice predates current approved safety cans. Does not address propane or kerosene.
conflicts: None.
editorial_note: Grounds the Z13-P60 vapour path and outdoor storage location.

locator: Power Outages: safety tips on generators, carbon monoxide, food, surges and extreme temperatures
conditions: Household power outages
support: Use generators, camp stoves and charcoal grills only outdoors and at least 20 feet from windows, doors and attached garages; do not use a gas stove or oven to heat a home; install CO detectors on every level; keep the refrigerator and freezer closed (refrigerator about 4 hours, full freezer about 48 hours); disconnect appliances and electronics against surges; go to a community location with power if heat or cold is extreme.
limitations: General guidance; the page does not mention candles. Generator connections follow the manual and licensed electricians.
conflicts: None.
editorial_note: Grounds the Z15-P43 layout and the Z13-P20 relocation step.

locator: Carbon Monoxide Questions and Answers: CO alarm installation and maintenance; fuel-burning equipment indoors
conditions: Home CO alarms and improvised indoor heat
support: Install battery-operated or battery-backup CO alarms on every level and outside sleeping areas, not in kitchens, above fuel-burning appliances or near heating vents; the test button checks circuitry, not sensor accuracy; alarms have a recommended replacement age from the manufacturer. Never use gas ranges, ovens or clothes dryers to heat a home; never burn charcoal inside a home, garage, vehicle or tent; never use portable fuel-burning camping equipment indoors unless it is designed for enclosed spaces.
limitations: No fixed alarm lifespan; follow manufacturer instructions.
conflicts: The CO-alarm lifespan in years on Z13-P56 is not on this page.
editorial_note: Grounds Z13-P56 placement and the Z13-P20 indoor-heat prohibitions.
reviewer: Fire prevention and carbon monoxide safety

locator: What to do During a Tornado: At Your Workplace or School; vehicles
conditions: Tornado warnings in workplaces, schools and other large buildings
support: Follow the tornado drill and go to the shelter location quickly and calmly; stay away from windows and do not go to large open rooms such as cafeterias, gymnasiums or auditoriums. At home use a basement, safe room or interior room away from windows. Being in a vehicle during a tornado is not safe.
limitations: The page does not describe wide-span roof collapse mechanics or specific building types such as stores.
conflicts: None.
editorial_note: Grounds the Z15-P18 floor-plan relationships.

locator: Outdoor Warning Sirens: Frequently Asked Questions
conditions: Relying on outdoor sirens for warnings indoors or at night
support: Sirens are an outdoor warning system designed only to alert those who are outside that something dangerous is approaching. For alerts indoors, every home and business should have a NOAA Weather Radio All-Hazards.

locator: Flood Warning VS. Watch: watch, warning, flash flood warning and advisory definitions
conditions: Interpreting NWS flood alert tiers
support: A watch is issued when conditions are favorable for a hazardous event; a warning when it is imminent or already happening; a Flash Flood Warning when a flash flood is imminent or occurring (move to high ground); an advisory when an event may become a nuisance. Flash floods can take minutes to hours to develop and can occur where it is not raining.
limitations: Flood products only; the Flash Flood Emergency tier is not defined on this page.
conflicts: None.
editorial_note: Grounds the Z15-P02 tier actions and the Z15-P23 flash flood timing.

locator: Storm Based Warnings fact sheet

support: Since October 1, 2007, tornado, severe thunderstorm, flash flood and marine warnings show the specific threat area as polygons that are not restricted to county or other geopolitical boundaries and can specify areas within a county.

locator: Flood Related Hazards: river flooding, flash flooding, ice jams, dam and levee failure
conditions: Flood mechanisms and their onset
support: Flash floods generally develop within 6 hours of the immediate cause and show a rapid rise of water over low-lying areas; river flooding occurs when rivers overflow their banks; an ice jam can act as a dam and release a flash flood when it gives way; dam failures or levee breaches can occur with little warning.

locator: Using Pressure Canners: dial-gauge accuracy, venting, pressure loss and canner size (Andress, 2014 revision)
conditions: Operating dial-gauge or weighted-gauge pressure canners
support: Check dial gauges for accuracy each year before use; replace a gauge reading more than 2 lb high or low at 5, 10 or 15 lb, and adjust when it is less than 2 lb off. Vent 10 minutes after a steady funnel of steam before pressurizing. If pressure drops during processing, return to pressure and restart the full original process time. Use a canner holding at least 4 quart jars, and raise pressure with elevation using reliable tables.
limitations: Does not give altitude pressures; who tests gauges is not stated on the page.
conflicts: None.
editorial_note: Grounds Z14-P55 and Z14-P56 gauge and restart relationships.

locator: Guide 1 pages 1-10 (equipment and methods not recommended), 1-30 (paraffin seals) and 1-35 (canner size)
conditions: Choosing canning methods and equipment
support: Open-kettle canning and processing freshly filled jars in conventional ovens, microwave ovens and dishwashers are not recommended because these practices do not prevent all risks of spoilage. Paraffin or wax seals are no longer recommended. The minimum pressure canner holds 4 quart jars upright; smaller pressure saucepans are not recommended.
limitations: The same 2015 page says steam canners are not currently recommended; later NCHFP guidance (P25) permits atmospheric steam canners within tested limits. Electric multicookers are not addressed.
conflicts: Steam-canner statement superseded by P25 for atmospheric steam canners.
editorial_note: Grounds Z14-P48 rejected methods and minimum canner size.

locator: Guide 1 pages 1-10 (altitude), 1-18 (boiling-water restart), 1-20 to 1-24 (gauges, timing and process tables)
conditions: Altitude, gauges and interruptions in tested canning processes
support: Water boils at lower temperatures as altitude increases and sea-level process times may cause spoilage at 1,000 feet or more; increasing time or canner pressure compensates. Process times are given in separate tables for boiling-water, dial-gauge and weighted-gauge canners; a weighted gauge moves to the next heavier weight above 1,000 feet (for peaches 5 to 10 lb). Weighted gauges control pressure precisely and need no accuracy check. If the water stops boiling, return to a vigorous boil and restart timing from the beginning.
limitations: Weighted-gauge steps are food-specific; read the tested table for the food.
conflicts: None.
editorial_note: Grounds Z14-P55, Z14-P56 and Z14-P57.
